pages.title: Selection controls · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Selection controls · HIG 0.1.0

Controls for choosing options, changing preferences, and adjusting values.

Includes Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, SegmentedControl, Select, and Slider. See the navigation guide for Tabs.

Issue #15. Entry: selection. Import platform entries from @bloxwap/hig-react/selection or @bloxwap/hig-native/selection according to applicability below. Import @bloxwap/hig-react/css once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

API and anatomy

Control Key props and behavior
Checkbox and switch checked, defaultChecked, and onCheckedChange. Native Switch also takes tone, a token role (action default, positive, negative, warning, info, buy, sell) for the on track; raw colours are not accepted and fall back to action. On Android the thumb uses the text token, so the app theme accent never shows.
Choice controls value, defaultValue, and onValueChange. Options have value, label, and optional disabled. Native options also accept description (a second line) and lang (the label's BCP-47 language).
Slider min, max, step, and value; a visible label is required. The DOM keyboard focus ring is drawn inside the 48px range box, so it never paints over the label or the next control at comfortable or compact density. Native increment/decrement actions use HIGProvider messages.increase/messages.decrease.

When to use and examples

Do: control selection from accepted host state. Don’t: emit a success cue on every render or repeated slider value.

Native language pickers can keep the native name and a translated description in one radio row:

<HIGProvider locale='en-US' fontFamiliesByScript={{
  latin: {400: 'BloxwapSansRegular'},
  ko: {400: 'BloxwapSansKRRegular'},
  zh: {400: 'BloxwapSansSCRegular'},
}}>
  <RadioGroup label='Language' value={language} onValueChange={setLanguage} options={[
    {value: 'ko', label: '한국어', description: 'Korean', lang: 'ko-KR'},
    {value: 'zh', label: '简体中文', description: 'Chinese', lang: 'zh-Hans'},
  ]}/>
</HIGProvider>

Register each face before passing its name. Text chooses fontFamiliesByScript by the label's glyphs, independently of the app locale; lang supplies accessibilityLanguage and resolves shared CJK punctuation. Descriptions use the app language. A script map selects the requested static weight, or its nearest registered weight; the existing fontFamilies/fontFamily remain the fallback. Explicit text script and style fontFamily override detection and registered family selection respectively. Native radios expose the label, supporting description as an accessibility hint, checked/disabled state and the explicit activate accessibility action; disabled rows reject both touch and accessibility activation. Per-option language is passed to React Native's accessibilityLanguage; pronunciation support depends on the platform and installed voices.

States, interaction and accessibility

Native HTML controls retain browser keyboard and selection semantics. RN Switch renders the OS track inside one labeled 48dp switch row (the row is the accessibility element and touch target); checkbox/radio use labeled Pressables with checked state. RN slider uses the optional community backend for the visual track and touch drag; a plain 48dp adjustable View owns the label, value and increment/decrement actions (5% steps) on iOS and Android because the backend's iOS Fabric view ignores accessibility increments and its Android SeekBar node measures 18dp. On Android the wrapper is the package's autolinked HIGAdjustableView, which also lists ACTION_SET_PROGRESS for Voice Access and Switch Access: a requested value snaps to step, clamps to min/max, updates the control once and is rejected while disabled. React Native's own accessibilityActions cannot express set-progress (custom names get synthetic ids and the progress argument is dropped). Without native linking (Expo Go) the wrapper is a plain View and set-progress is absent. The backend's native track height (18dp Android, 40pt iOS) still bounds direct touch drag; hosts needing a larger drag area should pad around the control. Select opens labeled native Modal choices and returns focus to its trigger.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

Platform mapping and limits

SegmentedControl is single-choice radio semantics, not navigation. Native picker alternative is deliberate. Accessibility increment/decrement, set-progress and disabled rejection are verified on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator (evidence/native-sim/); tactile drag feel and haptic rate remain physical-device work; backend is an optional native peer.

Validation and citation

See tests/components.dom.test.tsx, tests/native/components.test.cjs, tests/native/language-options.test.cjs, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.

SwitchRow from @bloxwap/hig-native/switch (also selection) wraps an existing host row in one switch target. It takes the same required label, checked / defaultChecked, disabled and onCheckedChange contract as Switch, plus required noninteractive children and root Pressable props. Keep the visible label, description and track noninteractive: the root owns activation and hides the content from accessibility to avoid duplicate targets. Put the description in accessibilityHint. Root style supports pressed callbacks; accessibilityState preserves busy while HIG owns checked/disabled state. Disable the row explicitly during pending requests; busy alone is descriptive. The Expo web row supports Space, Enter and pointer activation. Tree shaking an ESM import of ordinary Switch removes this optional anatomy.

pages.title: Status & feedback · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Status & feedback · HIG 0.1.0

Visible progress, notifications, and recoverable states that keep people informed.

Includes Badge, Alert, Callout, Toast, Progress, Spinner, Skeleton, EmptyState, Avatar, and StatusIndicator.

Issue #18. Entry: status. Import platform entries from @bloxwap/hig-react/status or @bloxwap/hig-native/status according to applicability below. Import @bloxwap/hig-react/css once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

API and anatomy

Component Key props and behavior
Badge Quiet label; web adds explicit tone (neutral, positive, negative, warning, or info), standard span props and a forwarded span ref. The neutral default retains its appearance. Tone uses provider token roles and never infers meaning from text or a number's sign. Badge adds no live region; the host owns announcements.
Alert title, severity, and an optional recovery action. Severity sets the accent edge from a token role on web and native: info → info, success → positive, warning → warning, error → negative. On native, tone swaps in another token role for an approved product accent, never a raw colour.
Callout Same API as Alert, for static guidance. It adds the documentation severities note (info role) and tip (positive role), so SDK docs do not need their own edge colours. Pass announce={false} for callouts present at page load. title accepts a ReactNode, such as text with a <code> span; on web it renders inside <strong> and should stay inline. On native it renders inside the Heading, so pass a string or inline Text; its visible text is announced.
Toast notices with stable id, message, severity, and optional action; onDismiss handles dismissal. Native notices also accept description and closable (default true when onDismiss is supplied). Native maxHeight bounds a scrolling viewport; it defaults to 60% of the window height and accepts dp or a parent percentage. dismissLabel overrides visible Dismiss text; its accessible name contains that text.
Progress label, value, and max.
EmptyState title, description, and an optional action.

Native EmptyState keeps the default Surface, Heading and body-text anatomy. Its description is optional; omitted or empty text leaves no blank description node. Pass decorative illustration content before the heading; HIG hides the whole illustration subtree from VoiceOver/TalkBack navigation while keeping the heading and action accessible. The host controls the illustration's dimensions and spacing. Root ViewProps, including style, testID and layout events, pass to the Surface. titleStyle and descriptionStyle reach the actual text nodes; maxFontSizeMultiplier caps both, or inherits the provider policy when omitted. Text keeps the provider palette and heading semantics unless the host explicitly styles it.

<EmptyState
  title={t('noMarkets')}
  illustration={<BrandMark width={64} height={64} />}
  style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', backgroundColor: 'transparent', padding: 0, gap: 12 }}
  titleStyle={{ fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 28, textAlign: 'center' }}
  maxFontSizeMultiplier={2}
  action={<Button onPress={clearFilters}>{t('browseAll')}</Button>}
/>

The mark and clear-filter action remain host-owned. tests/native/empty-state.test.cjs verifies default anatomy, omitted descriptions, decorative accessibility metadata, real text/root props and accepted action delivery; these wiring checks are not physical-device accessibility certification.

When to use and examples

Do: keep critical failure inline with Retry; use toast for copied acknowledgement. Don’t: dismiss critical text on a timer or rely on audio for success.

States, interaction and accessibility

Notifications deduplicate ids and preserve every message until explicit dismissal, including bursts larger than three. Host delivery queues may limit arrivals, but the renderer never silently removes an undismissed message. A single coalesced announcement reports each changed burst, prioritizing errors; unchanged rerenders do not repeat it. DOM and Expo web use one live region while every notification remains visible. Native Android uses explicit announcement delivery, and inline Android status uses live-region metadata; iOS announces changed inline content explicitly. Actual VoiceOver/TalkBack timing remains unobserved. Skeleton and spinner are static under candidate motion policy.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

Platform mapping and limits

Toast is an inline notification stack, no mandatory portal/timer backend. Host owns delivery ordering/persistence. On native, messages use body-size semibold text and descriptions use a separate body-size line; neither truncates or disables text scaling. The stack scrolls within maxHeight, including nested host scroll views. A notice with closable={false} has no Dismiss action; host recovery actions remain available. Without onDismiss, notices have no Dismiss buttons. No notice expires automatically: remove it from the controlled notices array when its host lifetime ends; keep failures with recovery actions until explicitly resolved. VoiceOver/TalkBack observations are pending, automated role/state tests are not device evidence.

// Native: compact notices with large-text scrolling and a persistent failure.
<Toast
  maxHeight={320}
  notices={[
    { id: 'saved', message: 'Saved', description: 'Your changes are ready.', severity: 'success' },
    { id: 'retry', message: 'Transfer failed', description: 'Check your balance and retry.', severity: 'error', closable: false },
  ]}
  onDismiss={removeNotice}
/>

Validation and citation

See tests/components.dom.test.tsx, tests/native/components.test.cjs, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.

pages.title: Optional adapters and installation · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Optional adapters and installation · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #22–#24. Base imports do not load adapters. Individual web-sound, browser-haptic, web-haptic, native and react entries preserve dependency boundaries. The composite web entry needs the Haptic package; sound-only consumers should import web-sound.

Web sound

Install @bloxwap/hig-feedback@0.1.0 @bloxwap/sfx@0.1.0. createWebSoundAdapter() loads SFX only for enabled requests after an accepted interaction. It calls the documented unlock/play APIs, passes per-call volume and uses the same presets as native. New requests replace pending startup, so delayed loading does not create a backlog. It avoids upstream global enabled/volume stores because HIG preferences are root-scoped. @bloxwap/sfx/react owns global preference helpers; using those alongside HIG would create competing preference owners.

HIG passes one adapter-local AbortSignal to each play. Muting, backgrounding, explicit cancellation and disposal abort that root's plays; the next accepted request gets a fresh signal. With the engine merged in sfx#51, this stops buffered and live voices while other roots and host-owned voices continue. Generations still discard superseded startup/unlock requests. HIG reference-counts default adapters and disposes the shared engine after the last user. A host that also owns that engine should inject/own its lifecycle.

Released compatibility: published @bloxwap/sfx@0.1.0 ignores the additional signal option. It remains compatible, and cancellation still prevents pending HIG playback, but its already-running voices continue. The signal-aware engine exists in merged source, not an npm release yet. Active-voice cancellation is forward-ready source support; released adoption remains pending in #70. No global stopAll() workaround is used.

Browser and physical-tap haptics

createBrowserHapticAdapter() maps accepted semantic events to browser vibration when navigator.vibrate exists. Its existing default and {vibrate} injection retain their patterns and work with published @bloxwap/haptic@0.1.0; neither imports Haptic. Device intensity/pattern quality varies and may be suppressed. iOS WebKit without vibration cannot provide imperative async outcome feedback; the adapter reports unavailable and remains silent.

The optional ImperativeHapticBackend injection accepts the exact canTriggerHaptic and triggerHaptic functions merged in haptic#30: createBrowserHapticAdapter({canTriggerHaptic, triggerHaptic}). These exports are absent from published 0.1.0; use the injection only with a host-owned source build until they ship. HIG probes capability at request time, so activation and document visibility are current, and delegates the semantic cue to upstream's presets. Rejection/failure cannot change the primary action. observed stays false. The adapter adds no eager import, helper DOM or physical-tap simulation.

The merged imperative API still reports iOS unavailable, including during transient activation. It cannot replace eligible physical targets or express iOS async outcome patterns. Neither the browser Vibration API nor this upstream API provides a per-root cancellation handle: cancel()/dispose() retain the existing navigator.vibrate(0) stop when available, which is document-wide. This is distinct from SFX's per-root voice cancellation.

For approved iOS physical action targets, install @bloxwap/haptic@0.1.0 and wrap a single ref-capable HIG button in HapticFeedbackTarget eligible. The wrapper uses upstream HapticTarget, preserves the target/handler/ref, enables only the physical-tap route and disables debug audio/helper switch visibility. Thus browser vibration comes from the semantic adapter and is not duplicated by the wrapper. HIG preferences still gate the wrapper.

Do pre-approve the target with eligible after disabled/busy/policy checks. Don't wrap an action whose eligibility is decided only by an async click callback, or promise a programmable iOS success/error pattern. The OS physical tick occurs before delegated handlers; a later preventDefault cannot retract that tick. That cancellation limitation, physical-tap intensity limits and device/VoiceOver checks remain upstream haptic#9 / haptic#7. The missing imperative iOS API for semantic controllers is haptic#27 (tracked in #70). No wrapper is required for basic actions.

Native audio

Install the feedback package plus expo-audio (~1.1.1 on Expo SDK 54, ~55.0.18 on SDK 55) only in the native host setup. expoAudioBackend(Audio) supplies a thin playback bridge; createNativeSoundAdapter(backend, assets) accepts Metro asset ids. The Expo gallery imports only the four committed WAV cues. Configure ambient/silent-mode behavior with playsInSilentMode:false, no background playback and doNotMix interruption mode. Host AppState calls setBackground; backgrounding pauses cached players. Call preload() at startup: it configures the audio session and caches players once. After that, play() dispatches synchronously, with no awaited bridge round trip before player.play(). It stops only the previous cue, issues seekTo(0) without awaiting it (native players apply calls in order) and plays. A cue requested before preload settles waits for it, and only the newest such request plays. Concurrency is limited to one active cue, volume/mute are honored, missing cues are silent, and disposal pauses/removes every cached player.

Playback completion: HIG does not listen to playbackStatusUpdate and never relies on didJustFinish. On Android, expo-audio 1.1 (Expo SDK 54) reports didJustFinish twice for one finished cue; SDK 55 (expo-audio 55.0) reports it once (#89). In the Android emulator run, SDK 54 had 4 play() calls, 4 playing starts and 8 didJustFinish statuses: the same finish reported twice, not a second play (evidence/native-sim/issue-86-88-89/). In expo-audio 1.1, every status sent while the player is ended carries didJustFinish: true, and two listeners send one when a cue ends. A host or future adapter that acts on completion must de-duplicate it, for example by ignoring a didJustFinish that has no play() or playing: true status since the last one. Device timing for both SDKs is tracked in #55.

Regenerate with npm run generate:cues. assets/manifest.json pins package/recipe/export flags, 48kHz mono PCM16, durations, peaks/RMS, bytes and reviewed hashes. Noise recipes vary; do not assert regenerated WAV bytes are deterministic. Inspect duration/envelope/level tolerances and review the actual artifact hashes. Offline generation dependencies are dev-only; Metro never imports them or browser synthesis.

Native haptics

Install expo-haptics (~15.0.7 on Expo SDK 54, ~55.0.18 on SDK 55) in the native host. expoHapticBackend(Haptics) bridges selection, impact light/medium/heavy and notification success/warning/error. createNativeHapticAdapter reports API availability separately from observation. Unsupported hardware, backgrounding, preferences and failed backend calls are no-ops that do not change primary actions. Android notification/impact approximation and OS suppression must be observed on devices before support is certified.

Simulated lifecycle regression evidence

Pinned, unmodified MIT source fixtures from SFX 1be6630 and Haptic 8b1ab578 test the adapters against the merged implementations, with source hashes and licenses in tests/fixtures/upstream-feedback/. The SFX tests use upstream's recording AudioContext fake to cover buffered/live root isolation, controller mute/background, cancellation during unlock, reuse and last-default-user engine disposal. The actual npm 0.1.0 package is separately tested to preserve playback and retain its active-cancellation limitation. Haptic tests use the actual merged capability/trigger functions with fake browser globals, cover changing activation/visibility, rejection, SSR and iOS unavailability, and preserve the released fallback. These tests request no physical sound or haptics.

The Linux tests inject native player and haptic backends. Pending configure/seek requests are superseded by the newest request; cancellation, backgrounding, zero volume and disposal stop pending playback. Failed configuration can retry. Explicit impact intent reaches the native backend even for an otherwise silent press preset. Pause/remove failures cannot prevent other cached players from being released. A dispatch test drives 400 cues through FeedbackController with simulated slow bridge calls (configure 60 ms, seek 40 ms). It asserts that every cue reaches player.play() inside emit() and that p95 stays under one 16 ms frame. The native gallery stamps each emit and logs dispatch/p95 on every play for simulator and emulator runs. These tests establish dispatch/lifecycle behavior, not observed sound, tactile output, acoustic latency (#55) or OS audio-session behavior.

Menu disclosure and dismissal are intentionally silent. Web/native Menu commits emit a single selection intent after the host handler; a host can cancel that effect with the selection event's preventDefault(). Native accordion disclosure emits one silent disclosure intent rather than duplicate activation/selection effects. The Chromium and WebKit fixture also checks switch, range, menu selection and canceled menu actions with injected adapters.

pages.title: Semantic feedback · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Semantic feedback · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #21, #25. Types in @bloxwap/hig-contracts/feedback and @bloxwap/hig-feedback import without DOM, RN, React, audio, Expo or hardware APIs. Base renderers accept an optional FeedbackSink; no provider or feedback backend is required to perform an action.

Intent Timing Sound Haptic Cooldown
press/release gesture phases; visual response silent none none
cancel discarded gesture/action; clears pending work silent cancel where possible none
activate accepted button click/keyboard/native press, after host handler tick selection 80ms
selection/toggle accepted state commit, never a render/repeated/rejected value tick/toggle selection 80ms
disclosure accepted open/close silent none 120ms
success host operation completion with stable operation id success notification success 400ms
warning host outcome silent notification warning 400ms
error host operation failure with visual recovery text error notification error 400ms
notification nonessential transient acknowledgement silent none 800ms

The exported presets table is authoritative. Each event has id, source, intent and origin. An async outcome uses the host operation id, not the button's interaction id; an accepted click does not imply order success. Optional native impact overrides map light/medium/heavy; browser physical-tap intensity cannot be programmed. Live price ticks and general navigation are silent.

Do emit a success event after the host request resolves, alongside visible success text. Don't play a success sound on press-in, for a rejected controlled value, or on every market render. Busy/disabled/suppressed/cancelled events are rejected. Buttons compose the host handler before activation, honor default prevention, preserve refs and block nested activation propagation. Choice controls emit on committed changes only. Sliders use semantic steps and controller cooldown; no effect queue accumulates. A host cancellation before activation suppresses the request; a physical cue already delivered by the OS cannot be recalled.

Preference precedence: host policy may forbid a channel; persisted user choices enable sound/haptics independently; component suppression can disable its request; OS/browser/backend capability decides whether output is attempted. Volume is clamped 0–1. Motion is a separate setting and OS reduced motion remains respected. Defaults are both channels off. No-feedback, sound-only, haptics-only, both, and host-injected adapter configurations use the same actions. Root/local FeedbackProviders hold independent preference/controller state; a nested button emits one request.

Deduplication uses source/id/intent; host stable outcome ids suppress repeated notifications. Cooldowns drop excess requests, never delay primary actions or queue a backlog. Seen/cadence maps are bounded. Exceptions thrown/rejected by backends and storage are caught. Disposal is idempotent and late startup/preload completions cannot revive disposed players. Capability available is API routing, while observed records actual physical evidence and remains false in this candidate.

pages.title: Preferences, preview and device review · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Preferences, preview and device review · HIG 0.1.0

FeedbackProvider accepts a stable createController(preferences) factory and optional storage adapter. useFeedback exposes preferences, update, sink and controller. FeedbackPreferencesControl is a render-prop control so DOM and RN use their own shipped Switch/Slider instead of importing another platform. Use a stable factory; mount/replay creates fresh adapters and unmount disposes them. React StrictMode lifecycle is tested.

jsonStorage supports browser Storage or native AsyncStorage-shaped interfaces. It uses a versioned key; read legacy saved choices explicitly with a host adapter before writing the new key. migratePreferences preserves explicit false sound/haptic choices, legacy soundEnabled/hapticsEnabled, clamped volume and independent reducedMotion/motion. Corrupt/missing storage falls back to muted defaults. A delayed saved read cannot overwrite a newer user choice. Storage rejection leaves the live UI usable.

Web and native fixtures include real independent sound, haptics, volume and motion controls, entry/selection/success preview and visible state. The web fixture persists localStorage; the native gallery persists AsyncStorage. Both wire lifecycle background state. Sound and haptic preferences are never encoded in wallet/trade logic. Native gallery sound import/package/Metro success is automated evidence, not audible/tactile observation.

Platform Routing Claimed observation
Desktop Chrome/Firefox/WebKit Web Audio after gesture; vibration only when API exists Automated interaction; no hardware assertion
iPhone Safari optional pre-approved physical target; async haptic adapter unavailable pending physical tap, VoiceOver, settings/OS review
Android browser browser vibration patterns when allowed pending device output/intensity
Native iOS/Android Expo audio and selection/impact/notification bridges pending physical output, latency and interruption review
Simulator / Jest mocks API/contract behavior only never tactile certification

Device acceptance record must include HIG/package versions, device, OS/browser, date, observer and actual observations: default/muted channels; each independent combination; volume/silent-mode; latency; interruptions; background/foreground; repeated/nested activation; cancelled scroll/drag; disabled/busy; slider repeated values; iOS preset limits; accessibility helper tab/VoiceOver order; visible recovery with feedback off. Attach video/measurements where useful. Reuse upstream haptic certification rather than declaring simulator passes as hardware proof. Owner: HIG and owning app/haptic maintainers, assignment pending; exception expires 2026-11-13.

pages.title: Trading glossary · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Trading glossary · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #46. Locked before any locale translation. Machine-readable source: docs/foundations/glossary.json (also exported as /hig/glossary.json). Formatting rules: localization guide.

Translation agents must consume the JSON. The rendered page is a view of that source. Do not invent terms, back-port product UI copy, or fill pending locales.

Locales

Locale Status Role
en-US approved Canonical English. HIG defaultEnvironment and authored documentation locale.
es todo No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/es.json in the product inventory.
fr todo No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/fr.json in the product inventory.
ko todo No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/ko.json in the product inventory.
ko-KR todo No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: Google Play store-screenshot locale in the product inventory.
zh-CN todo No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: apps/app/messages/zh-CN.json in the product inventory.
zh-Hans todo No HIG-approved glossary translation. Do not guess. Observed: App Store screenshot locale in the product inventory.
de-DE not a translation locale HIG Intl number-format fixture only. Not an approved translation locale.
ar-EG not a translation locale HIG Intl percent/numeral fixture only. RTL is a layout direction, not a glossary locale.

en-US is the only approved HIG glossary locale (defaultEnvironment.locale). Product message catalogs and store screenshots listed above are inventory observations, not approvals.

Change process

  1. Edit English fields in docs/foundations/glossary.json only. Do not hand-edit this Markdown.
  2. Run node scripts/generate-glossary.mjs (also invoked by docs generation) and commit the JSON and Markdown together.
  3. A term is locked when its English definition, usage notes, do/don't examples and untranslated flag are reviewed in this repository. Do not start translations before that lock.
  4. Promote a pending locale only by setting status: approved and supplying translations[locale] for every term. Incomplete locales stay todo.
  5. Never guess a translation. Product/marketing strings are not an approved glossary source.
  6. Changing a locked definition is a breaking content change for translation agents. Call out term ids in the PR. Tickers, brand names and untranslatedForms never enter translation files.
  7. de-DE and ar-EG remain Intl fixtures, not glossary locales.

This chapter blocks locale translation work until the JSON lock is adopted.

Terms

Perpetual (perp)

Term id: perp. Aliases: perps, perpetual futures, perpetual contract. Untranslated: keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: perp, perps.

Definition: A derivative that tracks an asset’s price with no fixed expiry. Funding payments help keep the contract aligned with its underlying market. Stocks, commodities, indices and pre-IPO listings on Bloxwap are perps, not ownership of the underlying asset.

Usage: Prefer “perp” in dense UI (market row, ticket). Use “perpetual” once in explanatory copy, then the short form. Never imply the trader owns the tracked stock, commodity or token.

Do: Label a Bitcoin market “BTC perp”. Say “open a perp position” rather than “buy Bitcoin” when the instrument is a perpetual.

Don't: Don’t call a perp a spot purchase, share, or tokenized stock certificate. Don’t invent an expiry date for a perp.

See also: funding, position, leverage.

Leverage

Term id: leverage. Aliases: lev. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales.

Definition: Position size relative to the margin supporting it. At 10×, 100 USDC of margin supports 1,000 USDC of notional exposure. Leverage magnifies both gains and losses. Market-specific limits are set by Hyperliquid, not by HIG.

Usage: Display as a multiplier with the multiplication sign (10×), never as a percent (1000%). Keep the × suffix untranslated. Limits and available leverage are host-supplied.

Do: Show selected leverage as 10× next to size. Repeat the selected leverage on the review step before the host submits.

Don't: Don’t write 10x leverage = safe. Don’t display leverage as +1000% or reuse percent styling.

See also: margin, notional, liquidation-price.

Margin

Term id: margin. Aliases: collateral, cross margin, isolated margin. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales. Untranslated forms: USDC.

Definition: USDC collateral used to open and maintain a leveraged position. If collateral falls below the maintenance requirement, Hyperliquid can liquidate the position. With cross margin, liquidation can consume the whole trading account, not only one position’s margin.

Usage: Bloxwap trading collateral is USDC. Say “margin” for trading collateral; do not call it a deposit held by Bloxwap. Isolated vs cross is a host/protocol mode, not a HIG component.

Do: Label available collateral “Available margin (USDC)”. Explain that cross margin can consume the trading account, not only the row’s margin.

Don't: Don’t call USDC margin a bank deposit or a Bloxwap-custodied balance. Don’t display unknown margin as 0.

See also: usdc, leverage, liquidation-price, position.

Position

Term id: position. Aliases: open position, exposure. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales.

Definition: Open long or short exposure in one market. A position has size, side, margin, leverage, entry, mark, notional, unrealized PnL and an estimated liquidation price. Closing requires a host-submitted order; HIG never executes a trade.

Usage: One row per market/side as the host provides. Don’t merge unrelated markets into a single position label. Size stays a raw decimal string in business logic.

Do: Title a row “BTC long” with size, leverage and PnL as separate readouts. Keep last-known position data and mark it stale when the host is offline.

Don't: Don’t say “position closed” until the host confirms the close fill. Don’t treat a formatted size as the order quantity.

See also: long, short, notional, pnl.

Liquidation price (liq. price)

Term id: liquidation-price. Aliases: liq price, liquidation, estimated liquidation price. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales.

Definition: The estimated mark price at which the position no longer meets its maintenance margin and Hyperliquid may force-close it. The figure is an estimate; auto-deleveraging can also close positions, including profitable ones.

Usage: Always present it as estimated and host-computed. Higher leverage generally leaves less room for an adverse move. Unknown estimates render as —.

Do: Label the readout “Est. liquidation price”. Keep the estimate visible next to leverage when the trader changes size.

Don't: Don’t call the estimate a guaranteed stop. Don’t omit “estimated” on first display in a risk-critical surface.

See also: margin, leverage, stop.

Funding

Term id: funding. Aliases: funding rate, funding payment. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales.

Definition: Periodic payments between long and short holders of a perpetual that help keep the contract aligned with its underlying market. Positive funding generally means longs pay shorts; negative funding means shorts pay longs. Funding is separate from exchange and builder fees.

Usage: Show the rate and the next payment time. Compute from UTC; display in the user’s locale with an explicit time zone. Hyperliquid funding is hourly; the interval is protocol-owned, not a HIG constant to restyle as a calendar expiry.

Do: Label “Funding +0.0100% · next 16:00 UTC”. Use a duration countdown (“in 12 min”) rather than a zone-less clock.

Don't: Don’t mix funding into the builder-fee line as if it were the same charge. Don’t show a next-funding time without a time zone.

See also: perp, pnl, long, short.

Profit and loss (PnL)

Term id: pnl. Aliases: P&L, unrealized PnL, realized PnL, net PnL. Untranslated: keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: PnL.

Definition: Profit and loss on a position or account. Unrealized PnL marks an open position; realized PnL is locked in after closes. Net figures may include trading fees and available funding; the host must say which components are included.

Usage: Keep the abbreviation PnL in every locale. Pair it with a signed, locale-formatted amount. Color is not a substitute for the sign. Zero is 0, not empty; unknown is —.

Do: Show PnL +$12.34 with signDisplay: 'exceptZero'. Name the readout “Unrealized PnL” or “Net PnL” according to host data.

Don't: Don’t translate PnL into an unverified local acronym. Don’t announce every live PnL tick to a screen reader.

See also: position, notional, funding.

Long

Term id: long. Aliases: UP. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales.

Definition: A position that profits if the market price rises. Opening long buys the perp; closing long sells it. Product chrome may label the action UP; the canonical term remains long.

Usage: Map UP/DOWN product labels to long/short in copy, APIs and accessibility names. Buy/sell color means direction, never safety. Don’t leave the canonical term untranslated just because the button says UP.

Do: Accessible name: “Long BTC”. Visible tap label may stay “UP” where the product uses it. Pair long with a buy-direction token, not a success/destructive intent.

Don't: Don’t say “buy Bitcoin” when the action opens a BTC perp long. Don’t use destructive red for every long close.

See also: short, position, perp.

Short

Term id: short. Aliases: DOWN. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales.

Definition: A position that profits if the market price falls. Opening short sells the perp; closing short buys it back. Product chrome may label the action DOWN; the canonical term remains short.

Usage: Same mapping rules as long. Short is a market direction, not a destructive action. Closing a short is not “selling the asset”.

Do: Accessible name: “Short ETH”. Visible tap label may stay “DOWN” where the product uses it. State “close short” for an exit, not “buy ETH”.

Don't: Don’t describe a short as borrowing stock or delivering the underlying. Don’t treat DOWN as a glossary synonym that replaces short in docs or APIs.

See also: long, position, perp.

Stop

Term id: stop. Aliases: stop loss, stop-loss, SL, stop order. Untranslated: keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: SL.

Definition: A reduce-risk order that submits a close when the market reaches a trigger the trader set. It is not a guaranteed fill at that price and it is not the protocol liquidation price.

Usage: Label the control “Stop”. If a compact badge uses SL, keep SL untranslated and expose “Stop” to assistive technology. Host owns trigger parsing and submission.

Do: Place stop beside take profit as optional risk controls on an open position. Confirm the trigger price as a raw string before the host submits.

Don't: Don’t present a stop as insurance against liquidation. Don’t reuse the estimated liquidation price as a silent stop.

See also: take-profit, liquidation-price, position.

Take profit

Term id: take-profit. Aliases: TP, take-profit. Untranslated: keep the listed short form in every locale. Untranslated forms: TP.

Definition: An order that submits a close when the market reaches a favorable trigger the trader set. Like a stop, it is not a guaranteed fill at that price.

Usage: Spell “take profit” in sentences. Compact badges may use TP; keep TP untranslated. Pair with stop; neither replaces a review step.

Do: Label the field “Take profit”. Show both trigger and current mark so the trader can see distance.

Don't: Don’t hide take profit behind an unlabeled TP icon. Don’t treat a take-profit fill as realized until the host confirms it.

See also: stop, pnl, position.

Notional

Term id: notional. Aliases: notional value, position value. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales.

Definition: Absolute position value in quote terms, typically mark × size. Notional is the exposure, not the margin posted. At 10×, 100 USDC margin corresponds to 1,000 USDC notional.

Usage: Use “notional” in Pro/details; “position value” is allowed in first-run copy if it still means mark × size. Never display notional as if it were withdrawable balance.

Do: Show “Notional 1,000.00 USDC” separately from “Margin 100.00 USDC”. Keep notional host-computed; HIG only formats the number.

Don't: Don’t label margin as notional or notional as available cash. Don’t round notional for display and feed that figure back into an order.

See also: leverage, margin, position.

Builder fee

Term id: builder-fee. Aliases: builder-fee, interface fee. Untranslated: no — translate in approved locales. Untranslated forms: bps.

Definition: A fee added by an interface that routes orders to Hyperliquid, charged on each fill in addition to the exchange fee. Live rates, Genesis discounts and rebate math belong to the host fee schedule, not this glossary.

Usage: Spell “builder fee”. Quote basis points as bps (untranslated) with a percent companion (5 bps (0.05%)) when showing a rate. Fees apply on open and close fills; funding is separate.

Do: Itemize “Builder fee” and “Exchange fee” on the review step. Point at the host fee schedule for the current rate rather than hard-coding it in a component.

Don't: Don’t call the builder fee a spread, a spread markup, or Hyperliquid’s exchange fee. Don’t bake a candidate rate into HIG component copy.

See also: funding, pnl.

USDC

Term id: usdc. Aliases: USD Coin. Untranslated: yes — keep English. Untranslated forms: USDC.

Definition: A stablecoin designed to track the US dollar. Bloxwap uses USDC for trading collateral and settlement. It is not the same ticker as USD for display purposes.

Usage: Always keep USDC untranslated. Format the amount with the locale’s decimal/grouping rules, then place the ticker USDC — never a $ or currency: 'USD' style. See the localization guide.

Do: Display 1,234.50 USDC. Use the Usd readout only for actual USD, not for USDC collateral.

Don't: Don’t localize USDC to “USD”, “US$”, or a local currency name. Don’t pass currency: 'USDC' to Intl; it is not a reliable ISO 4217 code.

See also: margin, notional, pnl.

pages.title: Numbers, currency, dates and built-in strings · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Numbers, currency, dates and built-in strings · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #47. Vocabulary is locked in the trading glossary; agents consume docs/foundations/glossary.json. Machine-readable format profiles: docs/foundations/localization.json. Host owns locale selection, parsing and time zone; HIG formats display only.

HIGProvider locale is a BCP 47 tag (en-US default). Direction (ltr/rtl) is independent. de-DE and ar-EG are Intl fixtures already covered by tests, not approved translation locales.

Shared helpers

Use the display helpers from @bloxwap/hig-contracts and the data readouts. Do not hand-roll separators, currency symbols, compact suffixes, the leverage × or zone labels. Every helper returns — for null, undefined and non-finite input.

import {formatNumber, formatLeverage, formatTicker, formatZonedTime} from '@bloxwap/hig-contracts';
formatNumber(value, locale, options);             // Intl.NumberFormat
formatLeverage(10, locale);                        // '10×' (decimal style forced)
formatTicker(12.34, 'USDC', locale, {signDisplay: 'exceptZero'}); // '+12.34 USDC' (no-break space)
formatZonedTime(instant, locale, 'UTC');           // '4:00 PM UTC' / '16:00 UTC'
Need API
Decimal/grouped numbers formatNumber / NumberReadout + host minimumFractionDigits/maximumFractionDigits
USD Usd (style:'currency', currency:'USD')
USDC formatTicker(amount, 'USDC', locale, options) — decimal amount plus untranslated ticker, never $
Leverage formatLeverage(value, locale) — 10×, never percent
Percent points Percent (5 means 5%; do not pass a ratio)
Signed PnL signDisplay:'exceptZero' on Usd/formatNumber/formatTicker
Compact totals notation:'compact', compactDisplay:'short'
Funding / expiry clocks formatZonedTime(instant, locale, timeZone) — Intl.DateTimeFormat with the zone name always shown
Other dates Intl.DateTimeFormat
Funding countdown Intl.RelativeTimeFormat on a duration, not a zone-less clock

Hermes in RN 0.81.5 and 0.83.10 provides Intl. Don’t polyfill, don’t concatenate '$'+value, and don’t parse a formatted string back into an order.

Numbers

Grouping and decimal marks come from the locale: 1,234.5 in en-US, 1.234,5 in de-DE, Eastern Arabic numerals in ar-EG. Precision is host-supplied (tick size, szDecimals). Generic USD balances may use 2 fraction digits; prices, sizes, funding rates and fees do not share one precision table.

Do keep 0 for zero and — for unknown/non-finite; mark stale. Don’t use a rounded display value as transaction input, strip unfamiliar separators, or replace Eastern Arabic digits with Latin ones unless a dual readout is explicit.

Currency, signed PnL and compact notation

USD uses ISO currency:'USD'. Intl places the symbol ($1,234.50 vs 1.234,50 $). USDC is a ticker, not a reliable ISO 4217 code: use formatTicker(amount, 'USDC', locale), which formats the number without style:'currency' and appends USDC after a no-break space. Never show USDC as $ or USD.

Signed PnL always includes a sign except at zero (+$12.34, -$12.34). Color is not a substitute for the sign. Don’t use accounting parentheses.

Compact notation is locale-owned. 1.2K / 3.4M is the en-US short form; de-DE yields 3,4 Mio., ja-JP may use 万. Never hard-code K/M. Compact is for overview totals, not order tickets or review amounts.

USDC PnL follows the same sign rule: +12.34 USDC. Tabular nums on every readout.

Dates, times and funding

en-US clocks are 12-hour (4:00 PM). Many other locales resolve h23. Use Intl.DateTimeFormat (hourCycle from the locale unless the host overrides). Store instants in UTC.

Funding and expiries: compute the next payment from UTC (Hyperliquid funding is hourly; the interval is protocol-owned). Display the instant with an explicit zone (16:00 UTC or a named device zone) using formatZonedTime. Pair a duration countdown (“in 12 min”) with that labeled clock. Perps have no expiry — don’t render an expiry field on a perp.

Don’t show a funding time without a zone or treat a local wall clock as UTC.

Leverage and percentages

Leverage is a multiplier with the untranslated × suffix (10×, via formatLeverage), never 1000% or percent styling. Percentages use the glossary’s rate terms (funding, builder fee as 5 bps (0.05%)) and Percent for percent-point values (+2.5%, -2.5%). Keep bps untranslated.

RTL and text expansion

Logical inline spacing, wrapping labels, no fixed-height clipping of translated text, Dynamic Type stays on. Plan for ~30–40% expansion (German/Finnish) and 200% text. Directional arrows mirror in RTL; brand, check marks and financial direction (+/−, buy/sell) do not. Preserve bidi isolates that Intl inserts around signed currency in Arabic. Mixed-script punctuation needs the required font scripts; a Latin-only fixture does not certify them.

Long translations, Arabic/Hebrew RTL and large text remain part of the platform checklist. Physical-device observations are still pending.

Native direction from the host locale

Issue #86. On native, HIGProvider follows I18nManager.isRTL when direction is unset. React Native 0.82 and later, including 0.83.10, do not report an Android per-app RTL locale through I18nManager (Android 13+ cmd locale set-app-locales ar-EG, or a per-app language picker). I18nManager.isRTL stays false, so an Arabic or Hebrew user would get a left-to-right HIG tree. RN 0.81.5 and iOS are not affected.

Hosts that lay out right to left pass the locale's direction:

import {getLocales} from 'expo-localization';
import {HIGProvider, localeDirection} from '@bloxwap/hig-native/provider';

const direction = localeDirection(getLocales()[0]); // 'rtl' for ar-EG; undefined keeps the I18nManager default
<HIGProvider locale={getLocales()[0]?.languageTag} direction={direction}>{children}</HIGProvider>;

localeDirection (also exported from @bloxwap/hig-contracts) returns expo-localization's textDirection when present. Otherwise it reads the tag's script, then its language: ar_EG, he-IL and az-Arab-IR give rtl; en-US, ar-Latn and en-u-nu-arab give ltr. It accepts BCP 47 tags, Android/Java identifiers and objects with textDirection/languageTag, and returns undefined for no language ('', und). Without expo-localization, React Native's I18nManager.getConstants().localeIdentifier is the app's configuration locale on Android (from the RN 0.83 source; the gallery verifies the expo-localization path).

  • Don't pass a locale-derived direction in an app that disallows RTL (I18nManager.allowRTL(false), or android:supportsRtl="false"). Leave direction unset so HIG follows the OS layout. HIG never derives direction on its own for this reason.
  • Don't expect I18nManager.isRTL to change on RN 0.83 Android. Native views HIG does not draw keep the host's direction.

Upstream: react/react-native#53417 (0.82.0) made I18nUtil.isDevicePreferredLanguageRTL read Locale.getAvailableLocales()[0] instead of the app's locale. The bug is reported in #54938 and fixed by #57635, first released in 0.88.0. 0.83.10, 0.84.1, 0.85.3, 0.86.3 and 0.87.1 still have the bug. The native gallery passes localeDirection(getLocales()[0]), and its os-arabic Android emulator step asserts rtl on RN 0.81.5 and 0.83.10 (evidence/native-sim/issue-86-88-89/). A system-wide Arabic locale and physical devices are not yet tested (#55).

Built-in component strings

Issue #62. HIG components render a small amount of their own copy: the Close button on overlays, the Toast Dismiss button, the Button busy suffix, loading and empty states, and the recipe labels. None of it is hard-coded in packages/react/src or packages/native/src. Every string comes from a typed HIGMessages catalog (@bloxwap/hig-contracts/messages). Hosts translate it through HIGProvider messages. A few components also take a per-instance prop (closeLabel, cancelLabel, dismissLabel, busyLabel).

HIG ships the English (en-US) defaults only (defaultMessages). It does not ship or guess translations. The host's message catalog owns French, Korean and other copy, under the same rule as the glossary: an unapproved locale is never filled by guessing.

import {HIGProvider} from '@bloxwap/hig-react/provider'; // or '@bloxwap/hig-native/provider'
import type {HIGMessages} from '@bloxwap/hig-contracts/messages';

const fr: Partial<HIGMessages> = {
  close: t('hig.close'),             // from the host catalog, e.g. 'Fermer'
  dismiss: t('hig.dismiss'),
  dismissNotice: (message, dismiss) => `${dismiss} : ${message}`,
  busy: t('hig.busy'),
};

<HIGProvider locale='fr-FR' messages={fr}>…</HIGProvider>
<Dialog closeLabel={t('checkout.back')} …/>   // one instance
<Button busy busyLabel=''>…</Button>           // no visible suffix; busy state stays exposed

Resolution order, per key: the component prop, then the nearest HIGProvider messages, then any enclosing HIGProvider messages, then English. A nested provider for density or direction keeps the host's translations. undefined keys and values of the wrong type (a string where a function is expected, or the reverse) are ignored, so a partial catalog never blanks a label. useMessages() returns the complete resolved catalog; useHIG().messages holds only the host overrides. Each English default is also a named export of @bloxwap/hig-contracts/messages, and a component falls back per key (messages.close ?? en.close), so importing one component bundles only the copy it renders.

Rules:

  • Visible text and accessible names come from the same key. The Close, Dismiss and busy text is the button content, so it is also the accessible name. The Toast dismiss name is dismissNotice(message, dismiss). A translation must keep the dismiss argument in it, so voice-control users can say the label they see. stale and required are appended to both the visible text and the accessible name.
  • A busy Button keeps its name (#94). When a native Button has text children and is busy, HIG sets its accessible name, because React Native Android otherwise announces only the busy state. On iOS the name is the visible {text} · {busy} (the text alone when busy is ''). On Android the name is {text}: Android appends its own localized busy state description, so the suffix would be spoken twice where the host's busy matches it (Korean 처리 중). An explicit accessibilityLabel always wins.
  • Slider actions are labeled (#87). The native Slider's increment and decrement accessibility actions carry increase and decrease. React Native 0.83 Android otherwise lists them with an empty label.
  • Close means dismissing an overlay. close closes a dialog or sheet. It is not the glossary sense of closing a position (an exit order). Translate it with the platform's dismiss word, never with the trading term for closing a position.
  • Functions receive formatted arguments. pageOf and progressValue receive numbers already formatted for the provider locale (Eastern Arabic digits in ar-EG). resultCount receives the raw count and the locale, so it can pick a plural form with Intl.PluralRules. Translations may reorder arguments. Component code never concatenates words.
  • RTL is a direction, not a translation. Messages render inside the provider's dir (web) or writingDirection (native). The Unicode bidi algorithm places the · busy separator and parentheses. Do not add direction marks to messages.
  • Trading words stay with the host. Default messages contain no glossary term. The TradeEntry recipe copy (reviewAssetOrder, confirmOrder, …) is generic order-review copy. The host supplies the asset ticker, which stays untranslated.

npm run lint runs scripts/check-built-in-strings.mjs, and so does tests/built-in-strings.test.ts. The check fails when a component under packages/{react,native}/src adds a user-visible or accessible literal. That covers JSX text, a visible or accessibility attribute (aria-label, accessibilityLabel, title, label, description, …), a label-like default prop and a set…() status string. To add copy, add a key to HIGMessages, read it with useMessages(), and add a row to the table above. The test checks that every key is in this table with its English default.

Validation

See tests/tokens.test.ts, tests/data.dom.test.tsx, tests/glossary.test.ts, tests/built-in-strings.test.ts, tests/messages.dom.test.tsx, tests/native/messages.test.cjs, docs/foundations/localization.json and the data chapter. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink.

The native Button's busy suffix starts with the separator (· Working); the row supplies its visual gap. On iOS its accessible name remains Action · Working. Android speaks the action name and its localized busy state once.

pages.title: Native runtime differences · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Native runtime differences · HIG 0.1.0

Follow-ups #86–#89 and #92–#94 distinguish implementation checks from physical-device certification in #55. The supported packed consumers remain React Native 0.81.5 / Expo 54 and React Native 0.83.10 / Expo 55. Historical simulator/emulator captures remain in evidence/native-sim/; their results are not overwritten by software tests.

Android locale direction

RN 0.83's I18nManager.isRTL can report false for an Arabic app locale. The regression is upstream #54938, introduced by #53417 and fixed by #57635, with older-Android handling in #58723.

HIG defaults direction to I18nManager.isRTL. Hosts that support RTL pass direction={localeDirection(getLocales()[0])}, using localeDirection from @bloxwap/hig-native/provider and their localization adapter (for example Expo Localization). This handles an Arabic per-app locale even when RN's OS diagnostic still reports false. Hosts that disallow RTL leave direction unset. Formatting locale remains independent, with en-US as the default. The Android os-arabic harness asserts the explicit host direction. Historical local fallback measurements predate the merged public API.

Slider action labels

RN 0.83 exposes an empty accessibility action label when the host omits it. HIG supplies messages.increase and messages.decrease for both actions, with English Increase/Decrease defaults and host translation overrides. Disabled adjustments remain rejected. Automated labels and state checks do not establish what a person hears through TalkBack; physical reference flows remain in #55.

iOS Dynamic Type audit

The historical RN 0.81.5 / Expo 54 run recorded 68 TextInput Dynamic Type heuristic findings. The RN 0.83.10 / Expo 55 run recorded none, while the large-text captures and text-field counts matched. The note in evidence/native-sim/native-sim.json applies to RN 0.81.5 only.

Source comparison of the release tags establishes that RCTUITextField.mm is byte-identical and the Fabric text-input view has no new UIFontMetrics/scaling behavior. The font utility changed to honor default font handlers in React Native #53755. That refactor has not been isolated as the cause of the audit change. We therefore do not claim a UIFontMetrics fix or a physical accessibility pass. Root-cause attribution for #88 and device VoiceOver/largest-size checks remain open.

Audio completion diagnostics

Expo Audio 1.1's Android playback status derives didJustFinish from the player's ended state. Both the playback-state listener and status polling can report that state. The SDK 54 captures show two completion callbacks after one recorded play:tick; SDK 55 shows one. A completion callback is not an extra play.

Only the gallery recorder listens to playbackStatusUpdate. The HIG adapter dispatches preloaded players without waiting for or replaying completion events. tests/native-verification.test.ts injects two completion callbacks and asserts exactly one backend play() call while preserving both raw diagnostic events. No runtime completion de-duplication is needed unless the adapter later depends on completion. Dispatch timing and audible latency remain distinct; speaker, silent-mode and interruption observations remain in #55.

Native text and color follow-ups

Native Button uses HIG Text for both its label and localized busy suffix, preserving font registration, script spacing and scale caps. Its busy accessible name includes the visible label, with explicit host labels taking precedence. Mixed ReactNode status titles concatenate visible text without inserting extra spaces.

HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3' selects the canonical P3 table on iOS. Android and web resolve to sRGB. Native controls and host-drawn views read the resolved table through useColors(); nested providers inherit the selected space. These are channel-selection and semantic tests, not comparisons of physical displays.

pages.title: Foundation and platform rules · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Foundation and platform rules · HIG 0.1.0

Color (#6)

Dark is the only audited mode. Source values retain the commit-pinned monorepo authored OKLCH and brand channels; see source reconciliation. Use surface/text/action/focus/buy/sell/warning roles, never infer intent from a hue. Web emits sRGB then P3 in @supports. RN uses explicit hex values from HIG's own tables, selected once per app by HIGProvider colorSpace (#93); see the native colour space table below. Android and third-party images use sRGB. evidence/contrast.json records all 33 approved normal-text pairings. Faint text is restricted to background/surface: faint on nested fails normal-text AA, so use muted on nested instead. Border is decorative; meaningful control edges/focus must use tested text or focus tones. Do use onAction on green fills; don't put white body text on green.

Native colour space

React Native reads a hex colour's channels in the app's default colour space. That is sRGB unless the iOS host overrides defaultColorSpace() in its React Native factory delegate to return Display P3. If it does, #ff5c5c is read as P3 channels and paints a more saturated red than the token. Set colorSpace on the root HIGProvider to match the host. Every HIG native component (Text, Surface, Separator, Button, Link, Field, Switch, Slider, Alert, Badge, Spinner, Skeleton, Dialog, GestureSheet and the brand mark) then paints from that table through useColors(). Hosts choose a table and never pass raw colours. Nested providers inherit the value, and a test fails if a component imports nativeSrgb or paints a raw hex value.

HIGProvider colorSpace iOS Android react-native-web
srgb (default) nativeSrgb nativeSrgb nativeSrgb
display-p3 nativeDisplayP3 (= nativeColors.iosDisplayP3) nativeSrgb (HIG publishes no Android P3 table) nativeSrgb
Role nativeSrgb iosDisplayP3
action / positive / buy / focus #00ff3f #00ff3d
warning #f5b300 #ebb63e
negative / sell #ff5c5c #ec6762
info #35b5ff #2eb8ff

Neutral roles (background, surface, nested, text, muted, faint, border, onAction) have the same hex in both tables. Use useColors() to read the resolved table for host-drawn views next to HIG components. Evidence is native Jest (#93) and iOS Simulator captures of the gallery built as a Display P3 host (evidence/native-sim/issue-93/). In the sRGB screenshots, display-p3 paints warning and negative as exactly the sRGB tokens (#f5b300, #ff5c5c), while srgb on the same host paints them oversaturated (#ffaf00, #ff4a54). Action and info are wider than sRGB, so the screenshot clips them. Physical display comparison is tracked in #55.

Typography (#7)

Pin @bloxwap/font 0.1.2. Vite: import @bloxwap/font/css; Next: upstream Sans/Mono loaders own loading and script fallback. Sans for prose/controls; Mono for code and tabular readouts; Pixel for a short nonessential accent. Body 16/24, label 14/20, caption 12/18, title 24/30, display 48/52 are candidate role mappings based on SDK scale. Web CSS exposes the roles as --hig-type-<role>-size, -line-height, -weight and a --hig-type-<role> font shorthand, and the families as --hig-font-sans/--hig-font-mono. Those resolve the @bloxwap/font Next loader variables first and fall back to the literal 'Bloxwap Sans'/'Bloxwap Mono' families, so HIG controls render the loaded face in both Next and plain @font-face hosts. Web rem uses 16px root; RN sizes are explicit dp and allow font scaling. Do not disable Dynamic Type or fixed-height clip translated labels. Run the pinned native font generator and register its static TTF faces from @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts; its typed manifest records weight/family/source hashes. Web hosts never install that package. Published WOFF2/Next loaders are not directly native assets. Do wait for registration before applying a custom native family; don't invent a family string and claim the font rendered. Arabic/Hebrew/CJK companions are owned upstream; load required scripts, test mixed-script punctuation and RTL. Large-text and device font evidence is pending.

Geometry and layout (#8)

Spaces 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/48; radius 6/8/10/14 and pill (--hig-radius-sm…--hig-radius-xl, --hig-radius-pill). Comfortable control/target 48 and gap 12; compact 36 and gap 8, reserved for pointer/keyboard dense layouts. CSS exposes each mode as --hig-density-<mode>-<control|target|gap>, and --hig-density-control, --hig-density-target and --hig-density-gap follow the nearest [data-hig-density], which the React provider sets. Painted icons can be 16/20/24 while targets stay 48 on touch. Never expand adjacent invisible hit areas so they overlap. Use logical inline spacing, wrapping labels, safe-area insets, keyboard avoidance and a scrollable native sheet; preserve portrait/tablet rotation without locking orientation. Pro tables may scroll with column headers; app amount entry reflows. Elevation uses nested fills rather than unverified shadows. Layer order: document, sticky nav, contextual popover, modal, notification. Browser top layer handles modal stacking; native Modal remains platform-owned.

Motion and gestures (#9)

Fast 180ms, base 260ms, slow 320ms; web easing cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). CSS exposes --hig-motion-duration-<fast|base|slow> and --hig-motion-easing-standard. The durations become 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and inside [data-hig-motion='reduced'], which the React provider sets when the host or OS asks for reduced motion. Press response ends on release/cancel; action executes on accepted activation, never press-in. Drag/scroll cancellation clears visual and feedback state. Interrupt transitions from current state instead of queuing. Reduced motion uses immediate state changes, static skeletons and unanimated numeric readouts. Outcome messages remain explicit. Do animate deliberate disclosure once; don't animate or play sound for every live-data update. Native candidate uses static transitions until cancellation/device animation evidence exists; motion preference is independent from sound/haptics.

Accessibility and localization (#10)

Baseline: WCAG 2.2 AA, Recommendation 12 December 2024. Normal text 4.5:1; large text and meaningful non-text UI 3:1. Touch baseline 48 logical units exceeds the web minimum. Provide visible focus, semantic labels/descriptions, logical keyboard order and non-drag alternatives. Native roles/state/value map to VoiceOver/TalkBack. No tooltip-only critical text. Restore trigger focus on modal dismissal; Escape/native back closes topmost cancellable overlay. Host owns safe-area, locale, parsing, route and keyboard adapters. Intl display is not money arithmetic. Vocabulary is locked in the trading glossary (docs/foundations/glossary.json) before any locale translation. Number, currency, date, leverage, percent and RTL formatting is in the localization guide.

Component review checklist: keyboard completion; labeled controls/errors; busy/disabled; focus restoration; narrow viewport; 200% text; long translations; Arabic/Hebrew RTL; mixed scripts; reduced motion; sound off; haptics off; unknown/stale/error values; VoiceOver/TalkBack on physical devices. Automated results and physical observations must be separate. Exception requires owner, affected surface, reason, alternative and expiry. No observed device evidence means pending, never pass.

Brand and icons (#11)

Approved mark is copied verbatim from the pinned Font docs SVG, including embedded provenance. Import @bloxwap/hig-tokens/mark.svg on web; both web and RN geometry renderers are available from their brand entries. Keep aspect ratio and clear space of one quarter mark width. Decorative marks/icons are hidden from accessibility; icon-only actions require an explicit accessible name and 48-unit target. Use currentColor for utility icons, never tint the approved brand mark arbitrarily. Directional arrows mirror in RTL; brand, check and financial direction do not. Icons repository contains a large catalog; do not import it wholesale. Only reviewed single glyphs belong in runtime exports. Favicon/OG derivatives have source provenance and drift checks. Physical device visual comparison remains unperformed.

Font-loading note: @bloxwap/font/css references all supported families/scripts, which may increase deployed asset bytes even with on-demand browser loading. The Latin web fixture instead uses two explicit @font-face rules with package asset URLs (Sans and Mono). Add only the scripts/italics used by each consumer. Do not assume a Latin-only fixture certifies mixed-script rendering.

Native text in multiple scripts

Register each required companion face with the host font loader, then pass its registration name through HIGProvider fontFamiliesByScript, for example {latin: {400: 'BloxwapSansRegular'}, ko: {400: 'BloxwapSansKRRegular', 600: 'BloxwapSansKRSemiBold'}, zh: {400: 'BloxwapSansSCRegular'}}. The provider's fontFamilies remains the fallback. Nested providers inherit the script map when it is omitted.

HIG Text detects Hangul or Han in each run even when the provider locale is English. Shared CJK punctuation follows the run's accessibilityLanguage, then the provider locale; script can select a face explicitly. If a script map has fewer weights, Text chooses its nearest registered weight. Explicit style.fontFamily wins. Hosts load these optional faces themselves; declaring a map does not load a font. Native RadioGroup options accept lang for the spoken label and description for its translated second line.

pages.title: Principles and content · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Principles and content · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #2, #3. Rules are candidate guidance anchored to SDK source and the public marketing surface; the pinned monorepo audit and live-origin snapshots are in evidence/issue-1-18/. Do not represent example trading actions as live product behavior.

Clear action hierarchy

Offer one primary action per decision. In an amount-entry recipe, do label the next step “Review order” and show the asset and amount before host submission; don't say “Go” or execute a trade when a field receives focus. Secondary actions navigate or cancel. Destructive intent means irreversible removal/cancellation; buy/sell colors mean market direction and never imply safety. Bind pending state to the host request, block duplicate activation, retain a progress label. Disabled means unavailable; busy means an action is running. Give the reason nearby.

Touch before density

Use comfortable 48-unit controls for mobile trade forms. Do stack amount, available balance, validation and primary action at narrow widths; don't squeeze a desktop order panel into a phone. Pro can use compact 36-unit controls with keyboard focus and separated targets. SDK code windows scroll horizontally; surrounding prose reflows. Marketing CTA and SDK install controls retain explicit labels, as observed in bloxwap.com and font/apps/docs/app/global.css.

State tells the truth

Resting, hover, focus, pressed, selected, busy, disabled, empty, error, success, offline and stale are distinct states. Do retain the last value with a timestamp and “Data unavailable — retry”; don't display unknown as zero, silently imply a completed order, or announce every price tick. Errors name the failed action and recovery. Confirmations repeat host-provided consequences and offer cancel before commit. Essential information remains visible and accessible with feedback muted.

Content and precision

Use sentence case and concrete verbs (“Copy install command”). Do display currency, precision and units supplied by the host; don't use a rounded display number as transaction input. Keep raw decimal strings in business logic. A percent component expects percent points, not an implicit ratio. Use localized display with explicit parsing policy; do not strip unfamiliar separators and submit a changed amount. Code uses Mono, body Sans, Pixel only as a decorative brand accent.

Composition and progressive disclosure

Show common actions first, advanced options on deliberate disclosure. Do give a native sheet a visible close action and let Android back dismiss; don't rely on hover tooltips on touch. Navigation remains host-owned: HIG does not choose routes, wallets, order types, or trading outcomes. Use status/callout for persistent critical errors; toast only for nonessential acknowledgements.

Concrete source and pattern references

The preceding rules map to Bloxwap-owned examples, without treating host demo outcomes as submitted trades:

  • Clear action hierarchy: pinned Bloxwap source, HIG pattern. Source primary/secondary/destructive variants, busy activation policy and semibold labels.
  • Touch before density: pinned Bloxwap source, HIG pattern. Source spacing aliases and 16-unit root; marketing CTA before-capture is before-bloxwap.com.png.
  • State tells the truth: pinned Bloxwap source, HIG pattern. Source notification severity and persistent readable outcomes; HIG preserves undismissed bursts.
  • Content and precision: pinned Bloxwap source, HIG pattern. Source display formatting stays separate from raw amount input and host arithmetic.
  • Composition and progressive disclosure: pinned Bloxwap source, HIG pattern. Source back/dismissal and safe-area behavior; basic HIG Modal alternative has an explicit close action.

pages.title: Pinned source reconciliation · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Pinned source reconciliation · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #2, #6–#9, #11–#18. See evidence/issue-1-18/monorepo-sha.txt for the exact monorepo commit and monorepo-source-fetch.json for all 129 audited paths. This supersedes the earlier 404 source-access limitation; it does not turn old unperformed product/device checks into passes.

The audit covers tokens, shared web/native primitives, plain-ui and app/Pro-owned controls. monorepo-audit.json records byte-identical duplicate groups, source bytes, repository asset totals and explicit source component dispositions. The existing catalog/platform matrix defines the HIG destination families. The authenticated organization inventory now includes monorepo, .github-private, taptradetv and tapsiren; their complete observed trees and explicit applicability decisions are recorded in new-repositories.json and planning/adoption.json. Named owner approval remains an organizational blocker, not a fabricated assignment. Confetti, signal strength, animated number backends and overlay layering internals stay optional host integrations; they are not silently added to base imports. Migration owners remain the owning product teams; HIG cannot claim their source forks have been deleted.

Tokens and platform units

packages/tokens/upstream-palette.json preserves the complete authored semantic OKLCH palette and brand sRGB/P3 channels. sourceColors exports web strings plus converted Android sRGB and iOS Display-P3 channel values; generated CSS exposes authored --hig-source-* variables. The HIG surface, nested, text and muted roles now retain their corresponding authored OKLCH values and tested sRGB fallback. Brand green and blue preserve upstream P3 channels. HIG focus green, market sell red, warning gold, opaque border and faint text are intentional intent/accessibility mappings rather than mislabeled exact source copies; direction remains distinct from destructive intent.

Native views default to sRGB and use nativeColors.android/ios. A host that explicitly configures RN iOS default color space as Display-P3 sets HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3', so HIG components paint nativeColors.iosDisplayP3 (also exported alone as nativeDisplayP3). It reads useColors() for its own views and converts third-party sRGB assets (#93). Never send CSS functions to native views or use P3 channel hex in an sRGB host. These are mathematical conversion checks, not physical wide-gamut display certification.

Source spacing.ts and type.ts explicitly set both rem roots to 16; native spacing md=12 and base type=16 match HIG. Radius 6/8/10/14 and motion 180/260/320 ms also match. HIG caption line-height 18, title 30 and display 52 intentionally provide readable role leading versus the stock utility steps. Comfortable 48-unit native targets and compact 36-pixel desktop targets remain distinct; compact native buttons still retain 48-unit hit targets. Source native sheets use optional Gorhom/Reanimated gesture backends, 320 ms card transitions and separate 500 ms opening motion. HIG's basic Sheet stays a static, scrollable Modal alternative. The isolated gesture-sheet entry now supplies an optional Gorhom adapter with detents, cancellation delegation, native back, safe-area/keyboard configuration, reduced-motion mapping and focus requests. Its mocked lifecycle and real Metro imports are software-verified; actual worklet, pan interruption and assistive-technology behavior still require a booted native target.

Native font generation and registration

Install fonttools[woff]==4.61.1 and brotli==1.2.0, then run npm run generate:fonts before native consumer commands. scripts/generate-native-fonts.py derives static faces exclusively from the installed @bloxwap/font@0.1.2 variable WOFF2 files, verifying all four input hashes before writing. It adapts the monorepo's generator and preserves its naming/weight metadata. The generated manifest contains input/output SHA256, PostScript names, Expo registration keys, weights, scripts and byte counts; OFL attribution ships beside the faces. Generated TTF files are build outputs, not per-repository committed binary copies. Local tarballs include them through @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/* (moved out of the web tokens package in #64); consumers register only needed faces.

The Expo fixture registers Sans Regular/SemiBold and Mono Regular through expo-font, waits for loading, exposes failure visibly and passes explicit 400/600 family keys to the native provider. Text, headings and buttons select registered static weight families, avoiding an invalid variable family name or synthesized weight. Expo web uses feedback.web.ts browser adapters; Android/iOS retain the native backend. Korean/Simplified Chinese Regular/SemiBold faces can be registered by host locale policy; other scripts use an explicit host/system fallback. Pixel remains a scoped web accent, not a native body-font requirement. Font registration in Expo web and Metro builds does not certify native rasterization, native Dynamic Type, or multilingual physical-device layout.

Observation boundaries

Headless browser synthetic composition checks preserve raw negative/decimal locale strings without formatting or precision loss; real on-screen IME composition is a separate device check. Browser 200% root text, narrow width and RTL checks exercise DOM reflow, not OS text scaling. Jest inspects RN roles, states and handlers with native modules mocked; Expo web exercises RN web rendering; neither is TalkBack. Android emulator installation, startup and any observed OS semantics are reported separately in evidence/issue-1-18/. Physical iOS/Android, tactile output and real VoiceOver/TalkBack observations remain unperformed on this Linux VM.

The root build now compiles contracts/tokens before feedback and platform renderers, so clean builds cannot rely on stale dist output. The expanded browser flow runs in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit under 320-pixel width, translated RTL tabs and 200% root text. It checks required validation, synthetic composition/raw precision, keyboard range/radio/menu/search, nested focus restoration, persistence/retry and zero automated axe WCAG findings. The Expo-web gallery separately checks registered faces, Modal picker, labels and range keyboard values. The native Slider web backend needs explicit ARIA min/max/now and keyboard actions; native OS builds retain adjustable role/state/value semantics. Checkbox/radio/tab web aliases likewise preserve native-renderer state in RN web. None of these observations is labeled as TalkBack. Quality gates verify every generated native face hash and cap the three selected fixture faces at 1.4 MB; optional CJK/other weight faces are available but are not imported by the default fixture.
