pages.title: Contribution, ownership and admission · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Contribution, ownership and admission · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #36. This chapter sets out how HIG stays the one maintained design system for Bloxwap. It covers who owns what, how changes are reviewed, how components enter and leave the catalog, which platforms are supported, and how a product can justify an exception. Release, semver and deprecation rules are in the release chapter. Setting up and upgrading a repository is covered in the new-repository chapter.

Canonical ownership

Area Canonical owner Others may
Semantic tokens (colour roles, space, radius, type, motion, density), native colour spaces, contrast pairs bloxwap/hig → @bloxwap/hig-tokens Map roles to host variables with var(). They may not redefine literal values.
Component contracts, DOM and React Native renderers, recipes, the semantic feedback contract bloxwap/hig → @bloxwap/hig-contracts, -react, -native, -feedback Compose components and override layout in context. They may not fork a primitive's paint or geometry.
Font sources, families and web loaders bloxwap/font → @bloxwap/font HIG generates pinned native faces from Font releases. Consumers install fonts and never commit binaries.
Sound recipes and the Web Audio engine bloxwap/sfx HIG owns the cue mapping and preferences, and exports approved WAV cues for native.
Haptic presets and the web engine bloxwap/haptic HIG owns the RN adapter and the capability matrix.
Chart engine bloxwap/chart HIG owns chart theming and the accessible non-canvas alternative.
Product business logic, routing and data The owning product repository HIG components never import wallet, network or trading code.
Brand marks bloxwap/hig brand component (pinned from the Font SVG) Use the component. Exact mark fills need a dated exception.

The organization adoption matrix (planning/adoption.json) records the owner, applicability, HIG version, merged PRs, status and dated exceptions for each repository and product surface.

Contribution and review criteria

Every HIG pull request must:

  1. Link its issue (Part of #N or Closes #N) and state its intent, the states it affects and its platform mapping.
  2. Change source and generated artifacts together, then run npm ci && npm run check (build, lint, generation drift, typecheck, web and native tests). Also run the smokes relevant to the change: smoke:ssr, smoke:packed, smoke:packed-native, smoke:packed-boundaries, smoke:packed-examples, examples:check and quality.
  3. Cover behaviour on both renderers, or record the platform decision and its supported alternative. Include accessible names, roles and states, keyboard and focus, native back, large text and RTL, and muted operation (sound and haptics off) without losing essential feedback.
  4. Label evidence precisely: automated, browser, iOS Simulator, Android emulator or physical device. A mock, simulator or emulator never proves physical sound, haptics, VoiceOver or display output.
  5. List the checks that were not run, upstream gaps, rollout and rollback. Breaking changes follow the release chapter.
  6. Pass the scoped anti-drift check (node scripts/drift.mjs, run by npm run quality and tests). New exceptions follow the exception policy below.

A maintainer reviews against the same list. A PR that only updates screenshots or baselines must say why the visual change is intended.

Component admission

A component or recipe enters the catalog only when all of the following hold:

  • It is used repeatedly in at least two Bloxwap surfaces, or one product surface plus an SDK docs site, and the inventory (planning/catalog.json) cites that usage.
  • It has a minimal API that composes existing primitives, with no wallet, network or trading dependencies and no unrelated imports. The per-entry export and boundary smokes enforce this.
  • It has a React DOM renderer and either a React Native renderer or a documented native alternative, and the platform matrix is updated.
  • It has a complete state matrix: focus, pressed, busy/disabled, error, empty, long text, large text, reduced motion, and feedback disabled where relevant. It also has catalog examples that typecheck in the packed consumers.
  • It is documented: a usage chapter, an API reference, accessibility notes and a migration note for each fork it replaces.

Component removal

  1. Inventory every consumer with org-wide code search and the adoption matrix.
  2. Deprecate the component in a minor release. Name the replacement, provide a codemod or checklist, and keep the export working for at least one minor release and 30 days.
  3. Open removal PRs in each consuming repository, or record dated exceptions for them.
  4. Remove the component in the next major release and record the change in the changelog and the matrix.

Platform support policy

Platform Supported (tested in CI or recorded evidence) Notes
React DOM React 19.2; Vite, SSR and Next 16.4 (webpack) packed consumers; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit Other bundler or Next versions need checks in the host
React Native RN 0.81.5 with Expo 54 and React 19.1.0; RN 0.83.10 with Expo 55 and React 19.2.0 (#68); Metro; packed Android/iOS exports in CI for both; iOS Simulator (iOS 26.5) and Android emulator (API 35) gallery runs for both RN 0.82 and 0.84+ are not supported. On RN 0.83 Android a per-app RTL locale does not reach I18nManager.isRTL, so RTL hosts pass direction={localeDirection(getLocales()[0])} (localization, #86). Physical devices are pending (#55)
Tokens only Plain CSS, Tailwind through host config, typed tokens No React, RN or audio peers
Feedback Web: @bloxwap/sfx and @bloxwap/haptic. Native: Expo audio and haptics adapters Essential outcomes must never depend on sound or haptics

Support only changes in a minor or major release. Each change updates docs/architecture/platform-matrix.md, the packed smokes and this table together.

Justified product exceptions

A product may differ from HIG only through a recorded exception. Silent forks are not allowed.

  • Scope: an exact path or folder prefix, and a single anti-drift rule (obsolete-import, copied-palette, copied-token-definition, copied-primitive-css or copied-font-binary).
  • Required fields: owner (an accountable role or person), reason (the user or product need, or the rollback dependency) and expires (YYYY-MM-DD, at most 180 days ahead).
  • Where: HIG's own exceptions go in planning/drift-exceptions.json. An adopting repository keeps its exceptions in its own hig-drift.json. The adoption matrix links to them.
  • Review: the check fails on expired exceptions and on exceptions without an owner or reason, and warns about unused ones. Renewing an exception needs a new reason and owner approval. Repeated exceptions for the same need are a signal to propose a HIG change through the admission criteria.

Intentional density differences, such as compact Pro versus the comfortable touch app, are HIG density modes. They are not exceptions.

Scoped anti-drift checks

scripts/drift.mjs has no dependencies and checks only files tracked in git under the configured paths. Paths listed under canonical are exempt from the copy rules.

Rule Fails when
obsolete-import Code imports a retired fork (@workspace/tokens, @workspace/ui, @workspace/ui-native, plus repository-specific obsoleteImports) or a copied vendor/hig/ or styles/hig/ folder
copied-palette Code hard-codes the Bloxwap brand hexes owned by @bloxwap/hig-tokens
copied-token-definition A stylesheet assigns a literal value to a --hig-* token. Remapping one role to another with var() is allowed
copied-primitive-css A bare .hig-* selector sets the primitive's paint or geometry (background, border, radius or min-height). Contextual layout overrides are allowed
copied-font-binary A .ttf, .otf or .woff* file is committed outside a canonical font owner

Generation drift (stale tokens, brand or glossary outputs) is checked separately by scripts/check-drift.mjs in npm run lint.

pages.title: New repository setup and upgrades · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
New repository setup and upgrades · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #36. These steps adopt HIG in a new or existing Bloxwap repository without copying component folders, palettes, fonts or feedback engines. The five SDK docs sites followed this path: bloxwap/hyperliquid#180, bloxwap/chart#53, bloxwap/font#11, bloxwap/sfx#50 and bloxwap/haptic#26.

1. Pick applicability

Add or update the repository's row in planning/adoption.json (a PR to bloxwap/hig) with one of these applicability values:

Applicability Install Never add
Product runtime UI (web) @bloxwap/hig-tokens, -contracts, -react; @bloxwap/font; -chart with @bloxwap/chart only for PriceChart (#96) Copied component folders or token CSS
Product runtime UI (React Native) @bloxwap/hig-tokens, -contracts, -native, -native-fonts; optional -feedback plus Expo peers DOM renderer imports, font binaries outside the manifest
Docs or marketing site @bloxwap/hig-tokens, -react (CSS and the controls in use); @bloxwap/font; -og-fonts as a build-time dev dependency for OG cards only A local .btn layer, a palette copy, vendor/hig, -native-fonts for OG cards
Brand or content only Nothing at runtime; follow the principles, content and brand chapters React, RN or audio dependencies
No UI Nothing; README and content conventions only Any HIG runtime dependency

2. Install versioned packages

HIG is not on npm yet (#56). Until it is, consume the packed candidate:

git clone https://github.com/bloxwap/hig && cd hig && git checkout <commit>
npm ci && npm run generate:fonts && npm run build
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel candidate   # local tarballs only; no publish, tag or release

generate:fonts needs Python with fonttools[woff]==4.61.1 and brotli==1.2.0. If you skip it, the release dry run, npm run quality and the packed font smokes stop with a message that names this step (#98). In the consuming repository:

  • Copy only the needed artifacts/release-candidate/bloxwap-hig-*.tgz files into vendor/bloxwap-hig/.
  • Record their SHA-256 hashes and the source commit in a README or provenance.json.
  • Depend on them with file: dependencies, adding overrides so HIG's internal dependencies resolve to the same files.

Never copy packages/*/src, dist folders, tokens.css, palettes, fonts or feedback engines. When #56 publishes, swap the file: dependencies for registry versions and delete vendor/bloxwap-hig/.

Then follow the installation chapter for your platform: import @bloxwap/hig-tokens/css and @bloxwap/hig-react/css once (add @bloxwap/hig-react/css/base first only when HIG owns the whole page), use per-component imports, load fonts through @bloxwap/font, and on native register fonts from the HIG font manifest.

3. Add the scoped drift check to CI

Create hig-drift.json in the repository root:

{
  "paths": ["apps/docs/app", "apps/docs/components", "apps/docs/lib", "apps/docs/styles"],
  "canonical": [],
  "obsoleteImports": [],
  "exceptions": []
}

Run the check from a pinned HIG checkout. The script uses only Node built-ins and needs no install:

- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with: {repository: bloxwap/hig, ref: <same commit as the vendored tarballs>, path: .hig}
- run: node .hig/scripts/drift.mjs --root . --config hig-drift.json
  • Scope: only paths you have migrated. Widen paths as more surfaces move.
  • canonical: use it only for assets the repository owns. For example, bloxwap/font owns its web font files.
  • Exceptions: record any other exception with an owner, a reason and an expiry no more than 180 days ahead, following the contribution chapter's exception policy.

First run against current main heads on 2026-10-15, scanning apps/docs (automated, local):

  • hyperliquid and haptic pass.
  • sfx flags the brand-mark fill in lib/og-card.tsx. That needs an exception like HIG's own brand marks.
  • chart flagged styles/hig-roles.generated.css (#66). chart#56 deleted it.
  • font flags its own font binaries, which belong under canonical.
  • agent-cli flagged vendor/hig/tokens.css, its import, and committed TTFs (#58). agent-cli#47 removed them, and its drift check now passes with no exceptions.

4. Validate and record

  • Build the site or app and run the repository's lint, typecheck, test and browser checks, plus keyboard, 390px mobile, large text and RTL checks.
  • Measure CSS, JS and font bytes and the dependency count before and after.
  • Link the merged PR, the HIG version and any dated exceptions in the matrix row.
  • Label evidence as automated, browser, iOS Simulator, Android emulator or physical device.

Upgrading HIG

  1. Read the changelog in the dry-run artifact, or the npm release once #56 is done, together with the semver section of the release chapter.
  2. Upgrade tokens, contracts, renderer and feedback together. Never mix candidate commits. Recompute the vendored hashes.
  3. Update the drift checkout ref to the same commit and run the check. Remove exceptions whose need has gone.
  4. Re-run the validation in step 4 and update the matrix row's higVersion and PR links.
  5. Roll back by reverting the upgrade PR, which restores the previous tarballs and lockfile. Product pilots also keep their host feature flag (for example NEXT_PUBLIC_HIG_PILOT=0).

pages.title: Quality, budgets and evidence · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Quality, budgets and evidence · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #31–#32. npm run check executes DOM and native suites with test counts. Native module mocks demonstrate roles/state/callback/lifecycle contracts; real packed Expo/Metro consumers demonstrate platform resolution. Neither is physical output or assistive-technology certification.

Gates inspect actual generated package exports, platform imports, tokens/cue hashes, scoped anti-drift exceptions, packed consumer installs, every copyable example, SSR/hydration/StrictMode, docs static route/base paths, visual/browser states and measured gzip/assets. Negative tests deliberately introduce invalid exports, stale token output, budget regression, cross-platform imports and copied/obsolete tokens to prove failure paths.

Budgets are regression limits from the initial candidate measurements, not claims of production savings:

Metric Measured initial Limit Reason
Individual DOM Button gzip (React external) 706 B 850 B ~20% API/behavior fix headroom, overlay/audio/chart excluded
Individual AmountInput gzip 325 B 400 B Small labelled primitive, ~23% headroom
Native Switch gzip (React/RN external) 1,383 B; 1,870 B after #67 2,200 B Raised for #67: the shared Text now carries the font-scale cap and Korean/Chinese script tracking, Switch the token-role track and the Android thumb token. ~18% headroom; verifies no Slider/SVG/overlay/feedback imports
Platform-neutral feedback contract gzip 962 B 1,200 B ~25% headroom without device engines
Docs JS gzip, all lazy chunks 204,877 B 240,000 B ~17% headroom; includes chart/code examples, not initial-load-only
Docs CSS 110,618 B (with token roles, #66) 115,000 B ~4% headroom; raised from 110,000 B when @bloxwap/hig-tokens/css gained radius/type/motion/density/font roles
Sans + Mono assets 592,796 B 600,000 B Pins two approved faces; new script/face requires explicit review
Native fixture faces from @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts (Sans 400/600, Mono 400) 1,278,880 B 1,400,000 B Only the three registered faces; optional CJK and other weights stay unloaded. Every generated face hash is checked
Font binaries in web/shared tarballs (tokens, contracts, react, feedback, native) 0 files 0 files Native faces ship only in @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts (#64); release:dry-run fails otherwise and records packedSizes
Native four-cue WAV assets 103,618 B 110,000 B ~6% headroom; no full engine/catalog assets

The actual build report is evidence/quality-report.json. The committed copy, the release report and the browser acceptance files were copied from a Linux CI run (evidence/ci-refresh.json, #98), not regenerated locally. GitHub Actions now runs on self-hosted macOS ARM64 Mac minis; see CI runners. Failed quality and browser jobs upload fresh copies for review; green runs skip the upload. Bundles use explicit external React/RN peers, so figures measure HIG runtime contribution, not total installed/Metro app size. Production app/Pro/native before/after deltas require owning-repository builds and reviewed baselines; do not invent a percentage improvement. Export/dependency graph reports and packed tests enforce separation, while owning migrations must measure complete apps with equal data/toolchain.

Exceptions require path/rule, owner, reason and expiry. Approved brand geometry is exempt from literal-palette detection until review; unrelated primitive/palette copies fail. New repositories should run scoped gates on migrated surfaces and keep dated residuals rather than blanket exemptions.

Physical release review remains pending: iPhone Safari, Android Chrome, native iOS and Android, VoiceOver/TalkBack, large text/RTL, color/font fidelity, actual SFX/haptic output/latency/settings/interruption/background behavior. Coordinate upstream haptic#9. Release artifacts cannot change those “pending” rows into passes.

Versioned visual regressions

The catalog browser gate captures and runs axe on every shipped state. Button, Field and Input additionally compare eight versioned mobile/reduced-motion screenshots in tests/visual-baselines/<process.platform>/ (linux or darwin), and Slider compares two keyboard-focused captures (comfortable and compact density). Geometry changes fail; pixel changes above 2% fail after a 24-channel-value antialias tolerance on every OS. tests/visual.test.ts deliberately changes geometry and pixels to prove the gate fails. Baselines record current candidate rendering on that OS, not approved product parity or native-device fidelity. Do not reuse another OS image or raise the thresholds to hide a runner difference. Review an intentional change using CI captures, then run HIG_UPDATE_VISUALS=1 node scripts/catalog-browser-smoke.mjs against the production docs preview and commit the reviewed baseline images for that platform.

pages.title: Release candidates, semver and rollback · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Release candidates, semver and rollback · HIG 0.1.0

Issue #32. This task's automation is dry-run only. It never invokes npm publication, GitHub release or git tag creation. Unsupported flags fail before artifact creation. No npm credentials are requested or used.

npm ci
npm run check
npm run examples:check
npm run quality
npm run generate:fonts   # Python with fonttools[woff]==4.61.1 and brotli==1.2.0
npm run smoke:packed
npm run smoke:packed-og
npm run smoke:packed-native
npm run smoke:packed-next
npm run smoke:packed-css
npm run smoke:packed-boundaries
npm run smoke:packed-chart-workspace
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel candidate
npm run release:dry-run -- --channel stable-simulation

Candidate mode stages 0.1.0-candidate.sha<commit> package metadata and matching internal dependency versions. Stable-simulation stages the coordinated source version. Runtime contract/docs source version and source commit are recorded explicitly; neither source files nor git refs are version-mutated by the dry run. Each dry run rebuilds packages and docs before staging so ignored output cannot retain an older API. Both produce local tarballs, checked export/types/CSS/assets/files/dependency manifests, hashes, changelog, copied docs artifact and provenance report. npm pack --ignore-scripts packs already validated outputs, never publishes. Physical claims remain pending in every report.

The release dry run, npm run quality, smoke:packed-native and smoke:packed-og first check that the generated TTF faces exist and match their manifests (#98). If any face is missing or stale, they stop before building anything. The message names npm run generate:fonts and its Python pins and lists the affected files, instead of failing with a raw ENOENT. packedSizes in the report records the packed and unpacked bytes and the font-file counts of @bloxwap/hig-tokens (no fonts), @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts and @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts. The dry run fails if any other package contains a font binary, or if @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts reaches 1,000,000 B packed (#99). smoke:packed-og builds the documented app/og/route.tsx handler with Turbopack (the Next 16 default) and with --webpack. It serves each build with next start, and also as moved standalone output. Every face's SHA-256 has to match, so a loader that bundles only one face fails here.

The chart adapter ships as its own artifact, @bloxwap/hig-chart (#96). The dry run fails unless @bloxwap/hig-chart declares @bloxwap/chart as a required peer and no other artifact names @bloxwap/chart in dependencies or peers. The result is recorded in chartAdapter in the report. npm run quality applies the same rule to the source manifests and to every built dist file. smoke:packed-boundaries checks that the packed hig-react manifest has no ./chart entry and no @bloxwap/chart peer, and that PriceChart renders on the server with its required peer installed. smoke:packed-chart-workspace builds a host shaped like bloxwap/chart: an npm workspace whose packages/chart provides @bloxwap/chart 0.3.0, plus apps/docs, which depends on it and on the packed hig-react, hig-chart, tokens and contracts through file: specs. The smoke deletes package-lock.json and node_modules and installs with legacy-peer-deps=false and strict-peer-deps=true. It then asserts four things. The lockfile keeps packages/chart and the node_modules/@bloxwap/chart link. npm ls is clean. Node and esbuild resolve @bloxwap/chart (including hig-chart's lazy @bloxwap/chart/react) from the app into the workspace. The host's HIGProvider messages reach PriceChart. It repeats the checks after npm ci and requires a second npm install to leave the lockfile byte-identical. Every scenario runs twice: once with the ambient npm (in CI, the npm bundled with Node 22.22) and once with the npm pinned in packageManager (11.6.1, the version chart reported), which is installed into a scratch prefix. A control run repacks hig-react with the old optional peer and records in evidence/packed-chart-workspace-smoke.json whether each npm still drops the workspace.

CI checks out PR source, installs locked peers, executes web/native/SSR/Metro/example/visual/accessibility/budget gates and uploads review artifacts. A provenance record identifies source commit, package/contract/docs versions and hashes; it is not an npm registry provenance attestation or a release. Artifact inspection checks exports, licenses, optional peers and only approved assets. No example app implementation is included in runtime packages.

Publication gates are tracked in planning/release-blockers.json:

  • npm credentials are not configured on the release machine (#56).
  • Physical devices and assistive technology (#55).
  • Upstream feedback gaps (#70).
  • Owning product migrations that are still open (#33, #35).

A dry run cannot turn these into passes, and renaming a candidate does not publish v1.

Semver:

  • Major: breaking changes to token meaning or appearance, typography scale, layout, accessibility or action behaviour, or semantic feedback mapping.
  • Minor: compatible additions.
  • Patch: verified fixes.

Deprecation names the alternative, a migration codemod or checklist, and the owning consumers from planning/adoption.json. A deprecated export keeps working for at least one minor release and 30 days, and is removed only in the next major release after consumer PRs are merged or have dated exceptions (see the contribution chapter). Keep code/examples/API/citations at the same source commit; separate package prerelease identifiers are explicit in artifact metadata.

Rollback for an owning pilot: keep the previous package artifacts and lockfile, disable the host feature flag, restore prior renderer/backend imports and rebuild. Keep saved feedback/business data backward-compatible; never erase prior choices. Remove old assets only after production and physical-device proof. A future published rollback would require separate release authorization and package provenance; this task performs none.

Maintainer-controlled registry publication (#56)

The local dry-run command remains unable to publish, create tags, or create releases. The separate publish.yml workflow is manual and accepts an existing version tag only. Before its publishing job can start, it requires configured reviewers on the npm-release GitHub environment and a successful candidate quality run for that exact commit. The environment then supplies the maintainer review gate.

The workflow rebuilds stable-simulation artifacts and runs release:verify: the tag, source commit and coordinated version must match; the complete eight-package set and every tarball hash must match; and all release blockers must be cleared or have a dated, named-owner approval link. Expired or undocumented exceptions fail. Uncommitted source changes fail. It never creates the tag or GitHub release for the maintainer.

An npm org owner must configure trusted publishing for each package name for bloxwap/hig, workflow publish.yml, environment npm-release, and approve the first registry version. The workflow pins npm 11.6.1 and Node 22.22.0, meeting npm's trusted-publishing requirements. Scope/name setup and any first-publish bootstrapping remain owner actions; no token is requested or stored by HIG tooling. Current local npm whoami returns E401 and @bloxwap/hig-tokens is not available from the public registry, so publication remains blocked.

Only after those gates does the workflow publish the exact verified tarballs with provenance. smoke:registry checks the registry tarball SHA-256 values and source-linked attestations, then runs independent web/SSR, Next hydration/font, and both native Metro/Expo consumers against registry versions. These registry checks have not been run successfully before publication. A failed post-publish check requires a maintainer response and a new version; automation never unpublishes or overwrites a registry version.

pages.title: Installation and citation · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Installation and citation · HIG 0.1.0

These are review candidates, not published npm packages. Use local dry-run tarballs or CI artifact downloads; do not assume @bloxwap/hig-* is available on the registry. Published-style imports in examples are tested against packed candidates. Version references identify a candidate until release gates are complete.

React / Vite

Run npm ci && npm run build && npm run smoke:packed. The smoke script installs tarballs into an independent temporary consumer and builds the fixture. For a host app install tokens, contracts and React tarballs plus React/DOM 19.2. Import @bloxwap/hig-tokens/css and @bloxwap/hig-react/css once; import individual components such as @bloxwap/hig-react/button. Pin @bloxwap/font 0.1.2 and choose only the required families/scripts using asset URL @font-face rules named 'Bloxwap Sans' and 'Bloxwap Mono'; HIG controls read --hig-font-sans/--hig-font-mono, which fall back to those literal families. The included fixture has Sans and Mono only, and its browser smoke checks that .hig-button and .hig-number render loaded Bloxwap faces. Never copy font binaries or component folders.

Component CSS and the opt-in base

@bloxwap/hig-react/css styles HIG components only. Every rule is scoped to a HIG class, for example .hig-button, .hig-table cells, .hig-range or .hig-surface[data-severity]. The box-sizing and focus ring rules use :where() on HIG classes, so they keep the specificity of a bare element rule and host CSS can still override them. Loading the file has no effect on plain table, th, td, input[type=range], [data-severity] or the focus outline of a non-HIG element. Hosts that load HIG on some routes only can rely on this: Next.js keeps a route's stylesheet after a client navigation, and the scoped file then has no side effects on the other routes (#95).

The page-wide element defaults are a separate, opt-in entry, @bloxwap/hig-react/css/base:

Rule Effect
* { box-sizing: border-box } Border-box sizing on every element
:focus-visible The 2px --hig-focus ring with a 3px offset on every focusable element
table, th, td Collapsed borders, full width, 12px cells with a --hig-border rule
input[type='range'] --hig-action accent, 48px minimum height, full width

Import the base only when HIG owns the whole page, and import it before the component CSS:

import '@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css';
import '@bloxwap/hig-react/css/base'; // optional: page-wide element defaults
import '@bloxwap/hig-react/css';

These are the rules that @bloxwap/hig-react/css applied to the whole page before #95, so a host that adds the base sees no change. The HIG docs site and the web and Next fixtures import it. HIG components look the same with or without the base. npm run smoke:packed-react-css checks this. It installs the packed tokens, contracts and React tarballs into an empty consumer and renders Table, Slider, Button and Alert to static markup. Then, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, it compares three script-free pages: tokens only, tokens plus @bloxwap/hig-react/css, and tokens plus the base and the component CSS. The plain table, cells, range, box-sizing, [data-severity] and keyboard focus outline must compute the same with the component CSS as with tokens only. The base page must change them, which proves the check can see a leak. The components must compute the same with and without the base. npm run smoke:packed-boundaries also checks that both entries resolve through package exports in a bundler and that the component CSS has no selector outside HIG classes.

Radix overlay peers and Fumadocs

The four Radix packages are optional peers with caret ranges: @radix-ui/react-dialog ^1.1.15, @radix-ui/react-popover ^1.1.15, @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu ^2.1.16 and @radix-ui/react-tooltip ^1.2.8. Install them only for @bloxwap/hig-react/overlay, @bloxwap/hig-react/recipes or @bloxwap/hig-react/recipes/trade-entry (dialog only). Hosts that already use Radix, such as Fumadocs, share their copy: npm run smoke:packed-fumadocs installs the packed React tarball next to fumadocs-ui 16.17.3 with strict peers and npm ci, asserts every @radix-ui/* package appears once, and renders the overlays on the resolved current releases. The workspace fixtures keep testing the lower bounds. Do not set legacy-peer-deps for HIG.

The separate optional @bloxwap/hig-react/gesture-sheet entry requires vaul ^1.1.2; Vaul brings its Radix Dialog dependency. Ordinary overlay and action entries do not load Vaul. Retain the host's existing input repositioning, handle-only, background scaling and viewport layout flags; see gesture sheet composition. npm run smoke:packed-boundaries verifies both absence in core consumers and resolution of the gesture entry after the explicit backend install.

SSR and Next client boundaries

Run npm run smoke:ssr, npm run build:next and npm run smoke:packed-next. Token/formatting imports and button/provider SSR are deterministic. Components with hooks carry use client in their emitted modules. In Next, import HIG CSS in the app layout (or in the route layouts that use HIG; the component CSS is scoped, see above) and put interactive example state in a client component; keep wallet/network logic with the host. Next's published Bloxwap font loaders remain owned upstream.

Fonts in Next: put the @bloxwap/font loader variables on <html>, for example <html className={${BloxwapSans.variable} ${BloxwapMono.variable}}>. The loaders register hashed family names, so HIG never matches a literal 'Bloxwap Sans' there. Instead --hig-font-sans and --hig-font-mono in @bloxwap/hig-tokens/css resolve var(--font-bloxwap-sans) and var(--font-bloxwap-mono) first and fall back to the literal families. No bridge CSS is needed. If a host keeps its own variable names, override the roles on :root after importing the tokens CSS: :root { --hig-font-sans: var(--my-sans), 'Bloxwap Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; }. The variables must be defined on <html> (not <body>), because the roles resolve on :root. npm run smoke:packed-next serves the packed consumer and checks, in Chromium, that .hig-button and .hig-number compute to a loaded Bloxwap face (document.fonts.check plus the FontFace status). Next 16.4.0 (webpack), React 19.2 and the published Bloxwap Sans Next loader are verified in the dedicated production fixture; other Next versions require host checks. Verify hydration, stable IDs and StrictMode before adopting a host version.

Open Graph card fonts

Satori, next/og ImageResponse and @vercel/og read TTF/OTF but not WOFF2, and @bloxwap/font ships only WOFF2. Docs and marketing sites that render OG cards install @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts as a build-time dev dependency. Do not use @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts for this (#99). The package holds five static Latin faces: Bloxwap Sans 400, 500, 700 and 900, and Bloxwap Mono 500. These are the faces the chart, sfx, agent-cli and tapsiren cards use. It packs to about 0.84 MB; the native fonts package is 4.4 MB. npm run generate:fonts copies the five faces byte for byte from @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts, so each SHA-256 in its manifest equals the native manifest entry. The release dry run records the packed size in packedSizes.ogFonts and fails at 1,000,000 B.

Node runtime (route handlers with export const runtime = 'nodejs', or static OG export scripts):

import {ImageResponse} from 'next/og';
import {loadOgFonts} from '@bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/node';

const fonts = await loadOgFonts(); // {name, data, weight, style}[]; throws if any TTF's SHA-256 differs from the manifest
export function GET() {
  return new ImageResponse(<div style={{display: 'flex', fontFamily: 'Bloxwap Sans', fontWeight: 700}}>Bloxwap</div>, {width: 1200, height: 630, fonts});
}

This works in a Next 16 route handler with the default Turbopack build and with next build --webpack. Turbopack copies the five faces into .next/server, so output: 'standalone' works even after you move it. webpack reads the faces from node_modules/@bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/fonts at the absolute path it had at build time. If a webpack standalone build runs from another directory, add serverExternalPackages: ['@bloxwap/hig-og-fonts'] to next.config. Earlier 0.1.0 candidate builds made each face's path from a template URL, and under Turbopack every face read the same file. The route then failed with BloxwapSans.ttf: SHA-256 f969fd1e… does not match the manifest.

Pass a subset if you need fewer faces: loadOgFonts(ogFonts.filter(f => f.weight >= 700)), with ogFonts imported from @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts. Edge and Workers runtimes cannot read node_modules at request time. Copy @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/fonts/<asset> into a gitignored build folder at build time. Before you write each file, check it against fontManifest.outputs[asset] (from the package root, or as JSON at @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/manifest), as tapsiren's copy-og-fonts.mjs does. Plain Node ESM scripts outside Next import next/og.js, because next has no exports map. npm run smoke:packed-og installs the packed tarball next to next@16.4.0 in a clean consumer. It hashes every exported TTF against both manifests and renders 1200×630 PNG cards through ImageResponse: each Sans weight must render differently, and none may match the default font. It also requires readOgFont to reject a tampered face. It then builds an app/og/route.tsx handler with the code above and checks it four ways: Turbopack and --webpack, each under next start; Turbopack output: 'standalone'; and webpack standalone with serverExternalPackages. Each standalone build is moved to another directory with the consumer's node_modules hidden. Every face must come back with its own SHA-256, and every card must match the plain Node render byte for byte. Results go to evidence/packed-og-smoke.json.

Expo / React Native

Run npm run smoke:packed-native after packed artifacts are built, or npm run start -w hig-native-fixture for the device gallery. Matrix: RN 0.81.5 with Expo SDK 54 and React 19.1.0, and RN 0.83.10 with Expo SDK 55 and React 19.2.0 (#68), Metro as locked. npm run smoke:packed-native -- --profile rn-0.83 installs the same fixture with the SDK 55 versions from fixtures/native/profiles.json; CI exports both consumers for Android and iOS. @bloxwap/hig-native declares react-native ^0.81.5 || ^0.83.10, so RN 0.82 and 0.84+ are outside the tested range. Native consumers install tokens/contracts/native tarballs; optional feedback installs its tarball and explicit Expo backend peers. Slider and SVG peers are only needed by their family entries. Import @bloxwap/hig-native/button, not the DOM renderer. Dynamic Type remains enabled; native targets stay 48. Keyboard/safe-area/back behavior belongs to the native host and its supported OS.

Install Expo native peers with npx expo install (for example, on SDK 54, expo-asset ~12.0.13 and expo-constants ~18.0.14 alongside expo-font/expo-audio; on SDK 55, expo-asset ~55.0.20 and expo-constants ~55.0.17). Expo 54 autolinking links the copy resolved from the app root; a hoisted SDK 57 expo-asset pulled by expo-audio's * peer compiles away and the app fails at launch with Cannot find native module 'ExpoAsset' (observed on the iOS Simulator). verifyExpoNativeModules in scripts/native-compatibility.mjs guards the fixture and packed consumer. HIGProvider follows the OS layout direction (I18nManager.isRTL) unless direction is passed. On RN 0.83 Android, a per-app RTL locale (for example Arabic set in the system's app language settings) does not set I18nManager.isRTL, so pass direction explicitly there (#86).

@bloxwap/hig-native ships one small Android library (android/, com.bloxwap.hig.HIGPackage) that React Native and Expo autolinking pick up in development and release builds (npx expo prebuild, npx expo run:android). It adds Android set-progress to Slider; nothing else depends on it, and in Expo Go the Slider falls back to increment/decrement only. iOS needs no native code.

Simulator/emulator verification: scripts/native-sim/ builds the packed candidate gallery as real Release apps and drives them with XCUITest (iOS Simulator) and UiAutomation instrumentation, uiautomator and TalkBack (Android emulator). prepare-app.sh <app-dir> <udid> rn-0.83 builds the RN 0.83 / Expo 55 gallery, and compare-runs.mjs compares it with an RN 0.81.5 run of the same candidate. Results and residual physical-hardware limits are in evidence/native-sim/ (RN 0.83: evidence/native-sim/rn-0.83/).

WOFF2 is not a native font asset. @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts ships 15 static Bloxwap Sans/Mono (plus Korean and Simplified Chinese Sans) TTFs generated reproducibly from pinned Font 0.1.2 sources, with a typed fontManifest export and @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/manifest. Install it alongside the tokens, contracts and native tarballs, then require('@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf') and register the faces with expo-font before setting the native provider fontFamily, as the gallery does. @bloxwap/hig-tokens no longer contains font binaries (#64); see native font migration. Rasterization on physical displays remains part of #55. New repositories follow docs/governance/new-repository.md.

Tokens only / plain CSS / Tailwind

Install the tokens tarball alone and import CSS variables or typed tokens. No React/RN/audio peer is required. Plain HTML uses semantic --hig-* roles.

@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css defines every role a plain CSS host needs, so nobody has to read the manifest or generate role files:

Roles Example Values
Color --hig-surface, --hig-action sRGB, then OKLCH/P3 in @supports
Space --hig-space-md xs–xxxl, section, in rem
Font --hig-font-sans, --hig-font-mono @bloxwap/font Next variable, then literal family
Radius --hig-radius-md, --hig-radius-pill sm md lg xl in rem; pill 9999px
Type --hig-type-body-size, --hig-type-body-line-height, --hig-type-body-weight, --hig-type-body caption label body title display; the bare role is a font shorthand in Sans
Motion --hig-motion-duration-base, --hig-motion-easing-standard fast base slow ms; 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce or [data-hig-motion='reduced']
Density --hig-density-control, --hig-density-compact-gap control target gap per mode; the unprefixed roles follow [data-hig-density='compact'] 
@import '@bloxwap/hig-tokens/css';
.card { border-radius: var(--hig-radius-lg); padding: var(--hig-space-lg); font: var(--hig-type-body); }
.card h2 { font: var(--hig-type-title); }
.card button { min-height: var(--hig-density-control); transition: background var(--hig-motion-duration-fast) var(--hig-motion-easing-standard); }

npm run smoke:packed-css proves this path. It installs only the packed @bloxwap/hig-tokens tarball into an empty consumer, links @bloxwap/hig-tokens/css from a script-free HTML page whose own stylesheet uses nothing but the roles, and checks the computed radius, type, motion and density values in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including 0ms durations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and [data-hig-motion='reduced'] and the compact values under [data-hig-density='compact']. It fails if the page requests anything other than the HTML, its stylesheet and the token CSS, so the manifest is never read.

Tailwind may reference these values through host configuration; HIG does not require content scans or a shadcn registry. Native uses dp and explicit hex/channel maps; do not feed CSS functions or rename rem to dp. The audited monorepo web/native rem roots are both 16; HIG supports StyleSheet rather than claiming a verified NativeWind consumer. See the source-reconciliation chapter for native font generation and registration.

Optional chart, sound and haptics

Chart is DOM-only and lazy. The adapter is its own package, @bloxwap/hig-chart (#96): install it with @bloxwap/chart ^0.3.0 (a required peer) and supply a textual summary. @bloxwap/hig-react has no @bloxwap/chart peer, so a host with a workspace @bloxwap/chart (like bloxwap/chart) can regenerate its lockfile from scratch with strict peers and keep the workspace link. See the charts chapter. Native uses labeled readouts/lists. Feedback install paths, preferences, iOS physical-tap limitations and Expo backends are in the feedback chapters. Keep essential outcome text available with both channels off.

Stable citations and upgrades

Cite “Bloxwap HIG 0.1.0 candidate, chapter/anchor” plus an immutable GitHub commit permalink. Branch and docs preview links are mutable. Upgrade tokens, contracts, renderer, docs/examples and semantic cue mapping together; compare API behavior and adopt behind a rollback flag. Token appearance and accessibility behavior changes require semver review. No publication, release or tag is performed by this implementation.

The native fixture pins React 19.1.0, matching the RN 0.81.5 renderer exactly; the RN 0.83 profile pins 19.2.0, matching the RN 0.83.10 renderer. Web/Next/Fumadocs fixtures use React 19.2.0. Metro explicitly resolves every native react/react/* import to the native fixture's version so shared-workspace code cannot load web React. Quality and packed-native checks compare the installed version to the version RN's Paper and Fabric renderers are built for (RN 0.83 no longer throws on a mismatch, so the check reads the renderer build itself); a successful Metro bundle alone does not prove runtime compatibility. The packed check also fails when a declared @bloxwap/hig-native or @bloxwap/hig-feedback peer range rejects a version the consumer installed.

pages.title: Native application pilot (#35)
pages.html:
Native application pilot (#35)

Owner: bloxwap/monorepo maintainers (named assignment in #57). Status on 2026-10-15: monorepo#4540 migrates the app's settings, entry, logout, sound card and demo number to HIG 0.1.0-candidate.shac32771dc, with one HIG feedback controller and 15 duplicate fonts removed. It loads the faces from @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts (#64) and passes translated messages (#62). It also drops the local Switch, Alert and Text workarounds (#67), and passes direction to HIGProvider on Android (#86). It was verified on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator and merged as 2f636e8fe on 2026-10-16. Physical-device certification is tracked in #55.

Workarounds the app can drop at its next candidate refresh (a candidate built from 74f4f6a or later; tracked in #115):

  • Busy Button name (#94): delete the HigActionButton wrapper's higButtonAccessibilityLabel. Button now sets the name itself: {label} · {busy} on iOS and {label} on Android, where React Native adds its own busy word, so Korean no longer reads 처리 중 twice.
  • Display P3 (#93): set colorSpace='display-p3' on the root HIGProvider and drop the local nativeColors.iosDisplayP3 lookup for the Button fill (see Native colour space).
  • Button text (#92): the label and busy suffix now follow the provider maxFontSizeMultiplier and use the 600 face. Re-capture the large-text and fr/ko screens.
  • Direction (#86): localeDirection from @bloxwap/hig-native/provider can replace the app's own direction lookup. HIG is certified on React Native 0.83.10 / Expo SDK 55 (#68). No tactile, audible or VoiceOver observation is claimed.

Pilot: font registration → dp/sRGB token mapping → amount/selection/review sheet → visible async outcome → independent feedback settings. The Expo gallery proves candidate packaging and contract examples, not the owning app's native build.

Checklist:

  • Record actual RN/Expo/Metro/autolinking versions, source commit, old ui-native/token/font/audio wrappers, screenshots and native bundle/assets/latency baseline.
  • Register the pinned static TTF faces from @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts and its typed fontManifest; register before setting family. Do not treat WOFF2 or an invented native family as success.
  • Map dp and legacy NativeWind rem roots explicitly. Keep Dynamic Type, 48 targets, logical RTL layout, safe areas, keyboard avoidance, native back and labelled fields/errors.
  • On RN 0.83, pass HIGProvider direction={localeDirection(getLocales()[0])} if the app supports RTL: an Android per-app Arabic or Hebrew locale does not reach I18nManager.isRTL (localization, #86).
  • Preview native import codemods, using individual switch/checkbox/range entries; wire optional SVG/Slider/Expo audio/haptic peers only where used. Retain platform-specific descriptions and host callbacks.
  • Preserve raw financial strings, order/network logic, stable list identity and quiet live numbers. Use labelled list/readout native chart alternative unless a real supported native engine is reviewed.
  • Read old sound/haptic settings with a host migration adapter before writing v1 key. Keep explicit false choices, volume and motion independent; handle corrupt/missing storage conservatively.
  • Hook AppState/interruption/background and dispose cached players/listeners. Test muted channels, missing assets, backend rejection, repeated values, busy/disabled, canceled scroll/drag and unsupported hardware.
  • Build the real app for iOS and Android. Observe large text, long translations, Arabic/Hebrew RTL, VoiceOver/TalkBack, orientation, keyboard/sheets, reduced motion and every feedback combination on devices.
  • Record actual device/OS/settings and audible/tactile output, latency, silent-mode/interruption/background behavior. Reuse upstream haptic#9 review; simulator/mocks remain API evidence only.
  • Remove duplicated source/assets/backend wrappers after device builds confirm references and autolinking are gone; quantify before/after sizes with equal toolchain/data.
  • Link owning rollout PR and remaining version/exception work into the matrix.

Native fonts moved out of hig-tokens

Issue #64. Up to 0.1.0-candidate.sha7c67a07c, @bloxwap/hig-tokens shipped the 15 static TTFs under @bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/*. Web-only consumers never served them, but they made up most of the tarball. They now live in @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts. The bytes, file names, registration keys and SHA-256 hashes are unchanged.

Before After
require('@bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf') require('@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/BloxwapSans.ttf')
@bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/manifest.json @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/manifest, or the typed fontManifest export
@bloxwap/hig-tokens/fonts/OFL.txt @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/OFL.txt
  • Expo / React Native: add the bloxwap-hig-native-fonts-*.tgz tarball next to tokens, contracts and native (with a matching overrides entry when vendoring), then replace the import prefix. nativeFont(fontManifest, 'BloxwapSans', 600) from @bloxwap/hig-contracts returns the registration key. Hashes you already pinned stay valid.
  • Satori / OG images in web repositories: these also read static TTFs (bloxwap/chart's OG card is one). Install @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts as a build-time dependency for that script only, or read the TTF from @bloxwap/font if it ships one. Never copy the faces into the repository.
  • Web-only hosts: remove nothing. They keep loading fonts from @bloxwap/font, and their tokens tarball shrinks. npm run release:dry-run fails if any web or shared tarball contains .ttf, .otf or .woff* files, and it records the packed sizes in packedSizes in the release report.
  • Coordination: monorepo#4540 (merged) already loads the faces from @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts.

Native colour space (#93)

Up to 0.1.0-candidate.shaac27cf7, HIG native components always painted nativeSrgb hex values. On an iOS host whose React Native default colour space is Display P3, those values were read as P3 channels, so the Switch track, Alert accent, Text, Surface and the other components painted warning, negative and info more saturated than the token. HIG now selects one of its own tables through the provider:

// iOS hosts whose app delegate returns .displayP3 from defaultColorSpace() (bloxwap/monorepo apps/mobile/plugins/with-ios-display-p3.js).
<HIGProvider colorSpace='display-p3'>{app}</HIGProvider>
  • Display P3 hosts set colorSpace='display-p3' on the root HIGProvider. iOS then paints nativeColors.iosDisplayP3, and Android and web keep nativeSrgb, so the prop can be set unconditionally. Nested providers inherit it.
  • Host-drawn colour next to HIG components: drop local nativeColors.iosDisplayP3 lookups and per-platform selection and read useColors() from @bloxwap/hig-native/provider. Delete wrappers that only existed to pass a P3 colour into Button style.
  • sRGB hosts change nothing. The default is srgb and renders the same values as before.
  • Raw colours are still not accepted. colorSpace takes only 'srgb' or 'display-p3', and any other value falls back to sRGB.

Rollback: host feature flag restores old renderer/backends and previous lockfile. Persisted business data and feedback choices retain old-compatible fields during staged rollout; avoid one-way preference deletion. Keep old static assets until both physical platforms pass.

pages.title: App, Pro and marketing pilots (#33)
pages.html:
App, Pro and marketing pilots (#33)

Owner: bloxwap/monorepo maintainers (named assignment in #57). Status on 2026-10-15: the first pilot is merged in monorepo#4515. Three follow-ups are open with green CI and verifier approval: #4522 (Pro compact density fix, navigation and numbers), #4523 (app Sound & Haptics controller) and #4525 (marketing waitlist, features and touch footer). They wait on the repository's required human signoff status. planning/adoption.json records the versions, rollback flags and gaps for each surface. The kit below is the checklist those PRs followed.

Surface Pilot and HIG mapping Preserve Owner work remaining
bloxwap.app Amount/field, review action, sheet/confirmation, account/feedback settings; comfortable 48 targets Raw amount/precision, wallet/network logic, busy protection, sheet descriptions, saved preferences and physical iOS tap eligibility Audit actual primitives/brand OKLCH, review import preview, migrate a host-flagged pilot, validate production/mobile/keyboard/feedback screenshots
bloxwap.pro Compact nav/order entry, market rows, numbers/table and optional chart Keyboard order, desktop density, sort/precision, chart pan/zoom/crosshair, live updates remain quiet Confirm legacy variants, wire host router and chart theme, compare dense before/after captures and per-component/representative bundles
bloxwap.com Hero/CTA/features, typography and plain CSS/tokens where appropriate Marketing content/links, metadata, static hosting and responsive CTA access Replace copied CSS/fonts only after consumers removed; build public site and compare representative pages/asset bytes

Checklist:

  • Pin HIG candidate artifacts/contract version and record source commit/baseline screenshots, CSS/font/duplicate/bundle bytes.
  • Run import-only codemod preview; inspect every diff. Do map brand→primary and danger→destructive after intent review; don't blindly map sell to danger or apply shadcn variants unchanged.
  • Preserve existing raw financial/business state; host validation still owns parsing and submission. No request on focus/open.
  • Wire explicit CSS/fonts/provider, comfortable app versus compact Pro, labelled fields and confirmation title/description.
  • Bridge legacy feedback preferences explicitly; never replace saved false choices with new enabled defaults. Physical tick must be pre-approved; async iOS outcomes can be silent.
  • Build the owning production app; verify keyboard, mobile, long labels, 200% text, RTL, stale/offline/error, muted channels and busy protection.
  • Compare before/after at the same viewport/data/toolchain; record measured source/asset/bundle delta without guessed improvements.
  • Remove old copies/dependencies only after reference search and build/device proof. Link owning PR and residual surface work in adoption matrix.

Partial adoption: scoped component CSS and the opt-in base (#95)

@bloxwap/hig-react/css now styles HIG components only, so a product can load it on the routes it migrates and leave the rest of the site alone. Next.js keeps a route's stylesheet after a client navigation. Before #95 the file also set page-wide rules (* { box-sizing }, a global :focus-visible ring, table/th/td and input[type=range] defaults), and these reached routes that never imported HIG. Those rules are now the opt-in entry @bloxwap/hig-react/css/base (see installation).

  • Whole-page adopters (bloxwap.app, bloxwap.pro, docs sites): add import '@bloxwap/hig-react/css/base' before @bloxwap/hig-react/css to keep the current look of plain tables, ranges and focus rings. HIG components need no change.
  • Partial adopters: import only @bloxwap/hig-react/css in the HIG routes, and delete any host reset that undid the old global rules. taptradetv loads HIG only on /sponsors (taptradetv#188, #59). It can drop the th, td reset in apps/web/app/sponsors/sponsors-hig.css once it moves to a candidate that contains #95. The /schedule calendar then keeps its own cell styles after a navigation from /sponsors, and non-HIG routes keep the host's focus ring.
  • Before removing a reset, verify with a client navigation from a HIG route to a non-HIG route in a production build. Compare the computed styles of tables, ranges and focus rings, not only screenshots.

Rollback: keep the previous artifact lockfile and original UI behind a host feature flag. Revert the pilot switch/lockfile; keep raw settings/business data unchanged. Do not remove legacy files until the pilot is certified. The adoption matrix, not this kit, records which surfaces are migrated.

pages.title: Five SDK documentation pilots (#34)
pages.html:
Five SDK documentation pilots (#34)

Owner: each SDK repository's docs maintainers (named assignment in #57). Preserve each interactive SDK demo and its host APIs; HIG replaces shared presentation only. Status on 2026-10-15: all five sites consume vendored HIG packages. Each was merged after independent verification: hyperliquid#180, chart#53, font#11, sfx#50 and haptic#26, all on 0.1.0-candidate.sha7c67a07c. Chart, SFX and Haptic then moved to 0.1.0-candidate.sha872906a9 in chart#56, sfx#52 and haptic#28. That refresh removed the workarounds for #63 (legacy-peer-deps and nested Radix trees; the overlay-free recipe entries are used instead), #65 (font bridges) and #66 (chart's generated role file). Hyperliquid and Font stay on 7c67a07c until their next refresh. Measurements and residual exceptions are in each PR's evidence folder and in planning/adoption.json.

Repository Shared presentation Distinctive feature to preserve Remaining owner validation
hyperliquid Font/tokens, shell/nav/search, code/install/copy/callout/forms/states Market playground and live SDK request handling Production/static export, query/deep links, market demo errors/loading, copy/search/mobile keyboard
chart Same shell/controls plus HIG chart theme Chart preview, drawings/controls, pan/zoom/crosshair and WASM/worker paths Canvas/text summary, gesture responsiveness, base assets, chart-specific demos remain optional
font Type roles, common controls/geometry and code windows Type tester, glyph coverage, variable axes and locale companions Font licensing/provenance, subsets/bytes, scripts/RTL/large text and tester functionality
sfx Controls/presets/settings/docs states Sound board and recipe editor/export Trusted audio unlock, mute/volume, edited recipes, native WAV command docs and cleanup
haptic Common controls and explicit capability labels Physical-target/platform demo and certification references Physical iOS/Android/VoiceOver evidence remains upstream haptic#9; no API-call-as-tactile-proof claims

Docs sites that render Markdown tables or plain form controls relied on the page-wide rules that @bloxwap/hig-react/css set before #95. On a candidate that contains #95, add @import '@bloxwap/hig-react/css/base'; before @import '@bloxwap/hig-react/css'; to keep the same look, as the HIG docs site does. See installation.

Per-repo checklist:

  • Pin source commit, HIG version and staged tarballs; capture before pages and duplicate CSS/primitive/font/audio/dependency/bundle baseline.
  • Inventory each existing apps/docs shell, static base path, metadata, search/index adapter, CSS/Next font loader and copy/install control.
  • Preview import mapping; preserve API props, router/search and SDK-specific business/demo logic. Plain HTML surfaces can use tokens/CSS alone.
  • Migrate one shared shell/control page behind a rollback flag; preserve Fumadocs conventions or host equivalent and existing deep-link/base URLs.
  • Execute that repo's production/static build and distinctive demo. Verify asset paths, keyboard/search/copy/mobile nav, loading/error/offline states, large text/RTL, and muted feedback.
  • Compare equivalent screenshots and measured CSS/font/runtime bytes. Remove old files only after references are gone and tests pass.
  • Update five separate adoption rows with owning PR URL, validated version, current gaps and rollback commit. Do not combine them into an unsupported “all migrated” claim.

Rollback: restore previous package lock/imports and shell flag per repo. Retain SDK demos and deep links. New shared HIG adoption must not change published SDK API examples.

Compact source comparison

The October 14 review of the five local checkout revisions found the following presentation baseline. These are source line counts, including product-specific styles, comments and formatting; they are not an estimate of removable CSS.

Chart, SFX and Haptic also repeat the same button and search recipes. Use the existing HIG token/component packages for shared behavior, and keep the written guide compact with rule → token or recipe → exception rather than duplicating the five implementations.

OG card fonts: switch to @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts (#99)

Since #64, chart, sfx, agent-cli and tapsiren vendor the whole @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts tarball (4,420,375 B, 15 faces) as a build-time dev dependency, but their Satori/next/og cards read only two to four TTFs. Switch each repository at its next HIG candidate refresh:

Repository OG card file Faces it reads Change

sfx apps/docs/lib/og-card.tsx Sans 700, 900 Replace both hig.resolve('@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts/fonts/…') reads with the same loadOgFonts call

tapsiren workers/tapsiren/scripts/copy-og-fonts.mjs Sans 400, 500, 700; Mono 500 Keep the build-time copy (the card runs on Workers). Resolve @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/manifest and @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/fonts/<face> instead of the native package; the SHA-256 values do not change

In each repository:

  1. Vendor bloxwap-hig-og-fonts-<candidate>.tgz from artifacts/release-candidate/ (about 0.84 MB packed; the exact size is in packedSizes.ogFonts of that candidate's release report). Record its SHA-256 next to the other tarballs in vendor/bloxwap-hig/.
  2. Replace the @bloxwap/hig-native-fonts dev dependency with @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts, regenerate the lockfile, and delete the native fonts tarball unless the repository also ships a React Native app.
  3. Import the fonts from @bloxwap/hig-og-fonts/node (loadOgFonts, readOgFont). These check every SHA-256 against the package manifest. They work with the default Turbopack next build and with next build --webpack. If the docs app uses webpack with output: 'standalone' and the build moves, add serverExternalPackages: ['@bloxwap/hig-og-fonts']. Vendor a candidate that includes the per-face asset URL fix. Under Turbopack, an earlier 0.1.0 tarball returns 500 with SHA-256 … does not match the manifest. An edge host checks fontManifest.outputs itself, as tapsiren does. Font names ('Bloxwap Sans', 'Bloxwap Mono') and weights stay the same.
  4. Rebuild the OG cards and compare them with the previous images. The faces are byte-identical copies, so the cards should not change. Record the vendored-byte delta in the repository's adoption evidence and update its row in planning/adoption.json.

See Open Graph card fonts for the full API and the edge-runtime path.

Chart adapter: @bloxwap/hig-chart (#96)

@bloxwap/hig-react no longer has a ./chart entry or an optional @bloxwap/chart peer. PriceChart and chartTheme moved unchanged to @bloxwap/hig-chart, which requires @bloxwap/chart ^0.3.0 as a peer. The optional peer made npm drop chart's packages/chart workspace when package-lock.json was regenerated from scratch without legacy-peer-deps. This reproduces on npm 10.9.9, 11.6.1, 11.21.1 and 12.2.0. A required peer does not trigger it.

pages.title: Documentation website and migration shell · HIG 0.1.0
pages.html:
Documentation website and migration shell · HIG 0.1.0

HIG uses Next.js static export and Fumadocs, matching the sibling SDK sites. SFX and Haptic pin fumadocs-core/fumadocs-ui 16.17.1, fumadocs-mdx 15.4.7 and Next 16.4.0; HIG uses those versions. Font uses 16.15.17/15.4.5/16.3.6 and Chart 16.15.14/15.4.5/16.3.6. React 19.2 satisfies the current Fumadocs peer contract.

docs/ Markdown chapters are the single normative source. The trading glossary is the exception: docs/foundations/glossary.json is authored and docs/foundations/glossary.md is generated. scripts/generate-docs.mjs generates the ignored apps/docs/content/docs collection, meta.json navigation, Markdown downloads, catalog data and llms.txt. Do not edit generated guides. Component reference pages derive from published package declarations and planning/examples.json; they link to the normative family guide. npm run generate:examples emits runnable web/native previews; npm run examples:check compiles all code variants.

apps/docs/source.config.ts defines the MDX collection; lib/source.ts supplies the page tree. app/docs/[[...slug]] renders Fumadocs titles, TOCs, code, navigation and source/edit links. components/provider.tsx and search.tsx provide the dark theme and static Orama search at search.json. Fonts, palette and preview controls import the shipped Bloxwap font and HIG packages. Fumadocs owns the responsive navigation, accessible search dialog and document shell.

Run npm ci, then bun docs:dev or npm run docs:dev. Turbo's terminal UI prepares package declarations, examples and guides before starting Next at http://localhost:3905/, with documents under /docs/. npm run dev:docs is an alias. Use bun docs:dev --ui=stream for plain terminal logs. bun docs:check and bun docs:build also prepare their required package outputs.

npm run build:docs generates the collection, builds Next and copies its static export to apps/docs/dist. Preview with bun docs:preview at http://localhost:4174/hig/. The static build defaults to /hig, while development defaults to the host root; override NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH without a trailing slash and HIG_DOCS_ORIGIN for another host. Every canonical document lives under /docs/. Explicit static redirect documents retain the previous /guides/*, /components/* and /catalog/ URLs, including their query and fragment. Sitemap, Markdown and LLM exports ship in the same artifact. No deployment is part of the build.

The homepage retains the bounded playground: App/Pro/Docs presets, supported states, locale/direction contracts, independent sound/haptics/motion settings, volume, matching Get Code, and validated share configuration. Native examples are real RN components in the Expo gallery. Device screenshots, VoiceOver/TalkBack and physical feedback observations remain pending. Live examples use sample host-owned actions and never submit orders or call a wallet.

Reusing the shell for issue #34

Each SDK keeps its own content and distinctive demo: Hyperliquid market playground, Chart preview, Font type tester, SFX sound board, Haptic interaction demos. Start with HIG's next.config.mjs, PostCSS/source config, lib/source.ts, root/docs layouts, provider/search and MDX component mapping. Set the product title, repository, base path and port. Copy the shell code as a starting template, then import the versioned HIG token CSS, React CSS and font assets rather than copying palette values or primitive implementations. Keep the SDK's existing content/docs as its normative collection, or generate it from one existing Markdown source as HIG does; never maintain two authored guides.

Place SDK demos behind a client boundary like components/demo.tsx; keep documentation server-rendered and searchable. Compose HIG install/copy/code/callout controls in those demos. Preserve each SDK's static search, llms.txt, sitemap, metadata and legacy URLs. Match the production base path during browser tests. Run build, lint, typecheck, example checks and the docs gates, capture desktop/mobile pages and the distinctive demo, and record exceptions and package versions in the #34 migration matrix. This HIG change provides the shell; it does not claim the five separate SDK migrations are complete.

Validation

npm run check includes the Next build and docs typecheck. CI runs production browser gates against the exported site, including the playground, search/navigation, legacy deep links, code tabs, all component states, runtime errors and axe checks. Screenshots and browser reports are uploaded with the static export as review artifacts. Publication, tagging and deployment remain separate operations.

The separate Documentation workflow builds and typechecks the static site for pull requests and pushes to main. After a successful build on main, it publishes apps/docs/out to GitHub Pages using the /hig base path. Pages uses GitHub Actions as its publishing source. This publishes the candidate documentation; package releases and tags remain separate operations. The workflow can also be run manually from main to redeploy.

The Fumadocs/Next framework changes the whole-export asset baseline: approximately 587 KB gzip of JavaScript and 95 KB CSS across all split routes (previous Vite budgets: 240 KB gzip and 22 KB). The new whole-export ceilings are 650 KB gzip and 110 KB CSS. This measures every chunk, not one page load. Font loading remains Latin Sans/Mono from upstream package files through next/font/local, avoiding the all-script loader’s roughly 13 MB export; the existing 600 KB font ceiling is retained.
